System A: Validated Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS)
Document Ref: URS-SYS-A-001 | Version: 1.0 | Status: Draft / Pending Review

document_title: System_A_URS.docx
content: System A is an enterprise Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS) utilized in QC analytical laboratories to manage sample registration, test execution, instrument integration, calculation verification, and batch release reporting. This system is categorized as GxP-Critical (Direct GxP Impact) pursuant to GAMP 5 Category 4 configured software.

document_title: System_A_URS.docx
content: System A must comply with 21 CFR Part 11, EU Annex 11, and ALCOA+ data integrity principles (Attributable, Legible, Contemporaneous, Original, Accurate, Complete, Consistent, Enduring, Available). All analytical data generated must remain immutable and subject to time-stamped, append-only electronic audit trails.

document_title: System_A_URS.docx
content: Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) must enforce segregation of duties between System Administrators, QC Analysts, and QA Reviewers. System Administrators shall not have privileges to alter or suppress laboratory test results.

document_title: SOP_Change_Control.docx
content:
Standard Operating Procedure: GxP IT Change Control
Document Ref: SOP-CC-004 | Version: 2.4 | Status: Effective | Effective Date: 2025-03-10
Review Cycle: Biennial | Next Review: 2027-03-10 | Owner: IT Quality Compliance

document_title: SOP_Change_Control.docx
content: This procedure establishes mandatory requirements for initiating, evaluating, approving, implementing, and testing changes to computerized systems utilized in GxP environments.

document_title: SOP_Change_Control.docx
content: All changes to validated software, hardware, or network configurations must be classified as Minor, Major, or Emergency. Major changes affecting GxP data workflows require full validation regression testing and formal QA pre- and post-approval.

document_title: SOP_Change_Control.docx
content: No GxP computerized system change may be migrated to production without documented approval from the System Owner and Quality Assurance. Automated changes or AI-assisted updates must be gated by human authorization.

document_title: SOP_Document_Management.docx
content:
Standard Operating Procedure: Document Management & Periodic Review
Document Ref: SOP-DM-001 | Version: 3.2 | Status: Effective | Effective Date: 2024-09-01
Review Cycle: Biennial | Next Review: 2026-09-01 | Owner: Global Quality Assurance

document_title: SOP_Document_Management.docx
content: Defines lifecycle controls for GxP documents including drafting, versioning, review, QA approval, distribution, and archival.

document_title: SOP_Document_Management.docx
content: All GxP documentation must undergo periodic review at least once every 24 months. If a document passes its periodic review due date without a formalized review extension or revised version, its status transitions to Overdue and non-compliant.

document_title: SOP_Document_Management.docx
content: Every GxP document must have clear author, reviewer, and QA approver signatures. Missing approval records invalidate document readiness.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-01-001]: Walk through the proposed intended use, the patient, product-quality and data decisions it will support, and the evidence used to draw the GxP system boundary before funding was approved.
Phase: Concept & Business Case | Domain: Governance | Topic: GxP intended use and system boundary | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Reconcile the business-case boundary with the process map, data-flow diagram, application inventory and any functions described as merely administrative; explain every mismatch.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Approved concept statement; end-to-end process and context diagrams; preliminary GxP assessment; named process/system/data owners; QA approval. Boundaries include interfaces, infrastructure, reports, records and supporting services and are internally consistent.
Regulatory Alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.1 and 211.68; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 Principle and §§1, 4.3; Guidance: WHO §§4-5 and 11.1.
Red Flags: No approved intended use; boundary omits reports, interfaces or infrastructure; GxP classification conflicts with process use; QA engaged only after funding.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-01-002]: Show how the concept team identified the predicate records, signatures, retention duties and inspection-access obligations for every jurisdiction and regulated business process in scope.
Phase: Concept & Business Case | Domain: Regulatory Compliance | Topic: Predicate-rule and jurisdiction assessment | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Choose a record the business case labels non-GxP and demonstrate why no batch, laboratory, complaint, stability, training or quality decision relies on it, including downstream exports.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Jurisdiction/predicate-rule matrix; record inventory; Part 11/e-signature applicability assessment; EU/other market assessment; legal and QA review. Each conclusion cites the governing requirement and downstream use. Acceptance: evidence is current, approved where required, complete for the selected population, and consistent with the live configuration and independent records.
Regulatory Alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.1-11.2 and 211 Subpart J; Binding EU legal framework: Directive (EU) 2017/1572 Art. 9; Guidance: FDA Part 11 Scope and Application.
Red Flags: Applicability based only on technology label; no predicate-record mapping; enforcement discretion treated as exemption; markets or retention laws omitted.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-01-003]: Describe the proposed data lifecycle from first capture through processing, review, reporting, retention and destruction, and show where the concept explicitly protects attributable, legible, contemporaneous, original, accurate, complete, consistent, enduring and available data.
Phase: Concept & Business Case | Domain: Data Integrity | Topic: Data lifecycle and ALCOA+ concept | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Trace one value that is transformed more than once and identify the original data, metadata, excluded or invalidated values, reviewer visibility and final record at every stage.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Preliminary data-flow and lifecycle map; data criticality register; ALCOA+ assessment; proposed technical/procedural controls; QA-approved gaps and funding. All transformations and review points are visible.
Regulatory Alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 211.68 and 211.180/188/194; Official EU GMP guideline: Chapter 4 Principle and §4.1; Guidance: MHRA §§3-5 and PIC/S §5.
Red Flags: Only final reports considered records; metadata/intermediate data absent; manual transcriptions not mapped; ALCOA+ cited without funded controls.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-01-004]: Demonstrate how the concept distinguishes source data, raw data, metadata, official records, convenience copies and hybrid components, and how the authoritative version will be identified during an inspection.
Phase: Concept & Business Case | Domain: Records Management | Topic: Authoritative record and raw-data inventory | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: For a proposed printout or PDF, show why it preserves—or does not need—the dynamic data and metadata required to reconstruct the GxP activity.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Preliminary record catalogue; record-of-truth decisions; hybrid-system map; dynamic/static assessment; true-copy strategy; ownership and inspection retrieval requirements, approved by QA and records management.
Regulatory Alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(b)-(c) and 211.180/194; Official EU GMP guideline: Chapter 4 Principle and §§4.1, 4.10; Guidance: FDA DI Q9-Q10 and MHRA §§6.6-6.11.
Red Flags: Final output declared the sole record without rationale; raw data/metadata ownership unclear; hybrid links absent; inspector-copy capability unfunded.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-01-005]: Explain how preliminary risk assessment differentiated patient-safety, product-quality and data-integrity harm, and how that analysis changed scope, controls, budget or schedule.
Phase: Concept & Business Case | Domain: Quality Risk Management | Topic: Data and process criticality | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Present the highest-rated data element and the highest-rated workflow; show the causal chain to harm and why a lower-rated neighboring item received less control.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Approved risk method; hazard statements; severity/probability/detectability rationale where used; critical data/process list; control decisions; residual-risk owners. Formality and evidence are proportionate to uncertainty and risk.
Regulatory Alignment: Guidance: ICH Q9(R1) §§3-5; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §1; Guidance: PIC/S §§5.3-5.6 and WHO §5.
Red Flags: Generic risk statements; unexplained low scores; detectability credited without a control; high risk accepted by project management alone; risk used to waive a binding requirement. Finding trigger: evidence is missing, unapproved, incomplete, inconsistent, or cannot be reproduced for the auditor-selected sample.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-01-006]: Show how the business case funds documented evidence that the system will remain fit for intended use across configuration, testing, release, operation, change and retirement.
Phase: Concept & Business Case | Domain: Validation Strategy | Topic: Lifecycle assurance and validation funding | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Identify an assurance activity removed for cost or speed and demonstrate, through risk and alternative evidence, why confidence in the intended use was not reduced.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Concept validation plan; lifecycle deliverables; risk-based assurance rationale; independent review; resource/skill estimates; environments and tools; acceptance gates; operational validation budget. Drug-GMP strategy meets predicate rules and Annex 11/15; device-only CSA is clearly scoped.
Regulatory Alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(a) and 211.68; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§1, 4 and Annex 15 §§1-3; FDA guidance (nonbinding, device QMS scope only): CSA §III and V.
Red Flags: Validation is a single pre-go-live test; no operational-state funding; CSA used to waive drug-GMP controls; estimates ignore interfaces/migration; QA approval not budgeted.

GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-01-008]: Demonstrate that the concept and procurement timetable allow risk-based supplier evaluation, technical assessment, audit where warranted, and remediation before supplier lock-in.
Phase: Concept & Business Case | Domain: Supplier Management | Topic: Qualification feasibility and evidence access | Priority: High
Follow-Up Probe: Show how the team would proceed if the preferred supplier refuses SDLC evidence, audit-trail design details, subcontractor visibility or regulator access.

content:

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-02-004]: Demonstrate how each URS statement expresses an observable outcome, boundary condition and acceptance criterion that can establish fitness for intended use rather than merely repeating policy words such as secure, compliant or user-friendly.
Phase: User Requirements (URS) | Domain: Validation Strategy | Topic: Testable requirements and acceptance criteria | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Select three high-risk requirements and show the positive, negative, boundary and failure-recovery evidence that could objectively prove each one before design is known.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Requirement quality checklist; measurable acceptance criteria; risk/test attributes; traceability conventions; verification method and responsible reviewer; approved ambiguity resolutions. Drug-GMP assurance is grounded in predicate rules/Annex 11, not a device-only CSA waiver.
Regulatory Alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(a) and 211.68; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§4.1, 4.4, 4.7 and Annex 15 §2; FDA guidance (nonbinding, device QMS scope only): CSA §V.A.
Red Flags: Subjective adjectives without measures; multiple controls bundled into one requirement; negative/error cases absent; acceptance delegated solely to supplier; CSA cited outside device scope to reduce evidence.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-02-005]: Describe the URS requirements that preserve the full record context—originator, event time, system time, units, status, method, version, reason and relationships—from first capture through every transformation.
Phase: User Requirements (URS) | Domain: Data Integrity | Topic: Metadata, contemporaneity and ALCOA+ requirements | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Choose one displayed value and show every metadata element needed to reconstruct who did what, when and under which configuration; identify where the URS requires each element to be retained and reviewable.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Data/metadata dictionary; ALCOA+ requirement mapping; time-zone and clock rules; contemporaneous capture; provenance and lineage; completeness rules; review and retention requirements; controlled rationale for any excluded metadata.
Regulatory Alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(e) and 211.188/194; Official EU GMP guideline: Chapter 4 Principle and §§4.7-4.9; Guidance: FDA DI Q1, MHRA §§6.1-6.7 and WHO §4.
Red Flags: Only visible fields specified; event and entry times conflated; time zone absent; metadata may be overwritten; lineage ends at report; ALCOA+ appears only in a generic preamble.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-02-008]: Demonstrate how the URS specifies unique attribution, role-based least privilege, joiner/mover/leaver timing, periodic review and ownership for human, service, interface and robotic identities.
Phase: User Requirements (URS) | Domain: Access & Security | Topic: Unique identity and least-privilege requirements | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Map the full lifecycle of one external contractor and one nonhuman account, including creation approval, credential storage, allowed transactions, monitoring, review and revocation.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Identity classes; authentication requirements; role/permission matrix; account lifecycle SLAs; service-account owner and secret controls; periodic review; inactive/terminated lockout; federation dependencies; traceable approvals.

content:

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-02-011]: Walk through each critical workflow and show how the URS requires permitted sequence, prerequisite evidence, role authority, status transitions and prevention or controlled override of out-of-order processing.
Phase: User Requirements (URS) | Domain: Workflow Controls | Topic: Operational, authority and sequence checks | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Attempt to approve before required data exist, repeat a completed step, use an unauthorized role and reopen a released record; identify the specified response and retained evidence for each.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: State-transition and use-case requirements; prerequisite/operational checks; authority matrix; override reasons/approval; duplicate/replay prevention; status visibility; exception/audit behavior; acceptance criteria.
Regulatory Alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(f)-(h) and 211.68(c); Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§5, 6, 12; Guidance: PIC/S §9 and WHO §11.
Red Flags: Happy path only; override unlogged; roles can self-approve; prerequisites described only in SOP despite configurable enforcement; released records can be reopened silently. Finding trigger: evidence is missing, unapproved, incomplete, inconsistent, or cannot be reproduced for the auditor-selected sample.

metadata.expected_evidence: State-transition and use-case requirements; prerequisite/operational checks; authority matrix; override reasons/approval; duplicate/replay prevention; status visibility; exception/audit behavior; acceptance criteria.

Red Flags: No unit/source validation; rejected values vanish; corrections overwrite originals; device identity not recorded; data-entry time substituted for event time; errors can be bypassed without reason.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-02-013]: Show how each interface requirement defines source and target records, field-level transformations, units/precision, identifiers, sequencing, acknowledgements, retries, duplicate control, reconciliation and retention of transmission evidence.

content:

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-02-015]: Explain how the URS identifies critical configuration and master data, assigns creation/change/approval authority, preserves effective versions and prevents unapproved values from influencing records.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-02-017]: Describe how the URS requires preservation or justified archival of legacy values, metadata, audit trails, signatures, status, links and record meaning, including reconciliation and handling of invalid or unmappable data.
Phase: User Requirements (URS) | Domain: Data Migration | Topic: Migration, conversion and legacy-history requirements | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Select a legacy record with corrections, attachments and signatures and trace each component to the target or archive, including how a user proves completeness after migration.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-02-018]: Trace every record category to a requirement for retention start event, period, archive format, metadata/audit history, readability test, legal hold, authorized destruction and documented evidence of disposition.
Phase: User Requirements (URS) | Domain: Records Management | Topic: Retention, archive, legal hold and destruction requirements | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Apply two different jurisdictional retention rules and a legal hold to the same linked record set; show how the URS prevents premature deletion of the record or its dependent metadata.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Approved retention matrix; event-based rules; archive/search/readability; linkage preservation; hold and purge authorization; destruction evidence; anonymization where applicable; supplier/default conflicts resolved.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-02-019]: Show how the URS specifies exact and complete backup scope, frequency, protection, separation, monitoring and periodic restoration with reconciliation to justified RPO and RTO.
Phase: User Requirements (URS) | Domain: Resilience | Topic: Backup integrity and verified restoration requirements | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Assume latent corruption, compromised administrator credentials and loss of the primary region; demonstrate the required recovery source, integrity proof and transaction-level reconciliation.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Backup objects include data, metadata, audit trails, configuration, keys and dependencies; justified RPO/RTO; immutable/offline protection where risk warrants; restore frequency; acceptance/control totals; alerts and retained test evidence.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-02-020]: Walk through URS requirements for controlled offline operation during application, interface, identity or site outages and for complete, duplicate-free reconciliation when service returns.
Phase: User Requirements (URS) | Domain: Business Continuity | Topic: Manual fallback and post-outage reconciliation requirements | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Simulate two sites creating the same identifier offline while an interface queues messages; identify the required numbering, timestamp, approval, conflict resolution and QA review behavior.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Outage scenarios; controlled fallback records; unique/offline identifiers; event versus entry time; authority and approval; queued-interface handling; reconciliation/control totals; exception/QA review; exercise and capacity criteria.
Regulatory Alignment: Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §16 and Chapter 4 §§4.7-4.9; Guidance: MHRA §5.1, PIC/S §9.9 and WHO §§4, 11.15-11.19.
Red Flags: Fallback is an uncontrolled spreadsheet; no offline numbering; event time lost; queued messages can replay; reconciliation lacks totals/owner; exercise requirement absent.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-02-021]: Explain how the URS converts the GxP threat model into requirements for authentication, encryption, secure configuration, vulnerability handling, event logging, clock synchronization, monitoring and protection of data at rest and in transit.
Phase: User Requirements (URS) | Domain: Cybersecurity | Topic: Security logging, time synchronization and data protection | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Trace a compromised support account changing the system clock and exporting data; show which requirement prevents, detects, timestamps, contains and investigates each action without losing GxP evidence.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Risk-linked security requirements; trusted time source and drift tolerance; security/audit log scope and retention; encryption/key ownership; secure baseline; vulnerability/patch SLAs; monitoring alerts; forensic preservation; remote-support controls. Acceptance: evidence is current, approved where required, complete for the selected population, and consistent with the live configuration and independent records.

Phase: Risk Assessment & GAMP Categorisation | Domain: Quality Risk Management | Topic: Risk method, governance and formality | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Reperform one high, one medium and one low decision with independent SMEs; explain score differences, assumptions and why the method would not allow an otherwise noncompliant control to be accepted.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Approved QRM procedure; trained cross-functional team; defined scope, scales and decision rules; evidence-based hazards; documented assumptions/uncertainty; independent QA review; escalation and risk-acceptance authority. QRM does not waive binding controls.
Regulatory Alignment: Guidance: ICH Q9(R1) §§3-5; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §1; Guidance: PIC/S §§5.3-5.6 and WHO §5.
Red Flags: One-person assessment; all scores cluster low; severity reduced because controls exist; detectability credited without evidence; project owner accepts quality risk; binding requirement risk-scored away. metadata.expected_evidence: Approved QRM procedure; trained cross-functional team; defined scope, scales and decision rules; evidence-based hazards; documented assumptions/uncertainty; independent QA review; escalation and risk-acceptance authority. QRM does not waive binding controls.

content:

content:

content:

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-04-015]: Show the exact backup scope, schedules, retention, isolation, encryption, monitoring and restoration process for tenant data, metadata, audit trails, configuration, files and keys.

Red Flags: Audit trails/configuration/keys excluded; restore tests are infrastructure-only; tenant restoration unavailable; backup shares admin domain; test exceptions not investigated; customer receives no evidence.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-04-016]: Demonstrate how the supplier derived and tested availability, capacity, RTO and RPO across application and external dependencies, and how customers are informed and supported during regional or prolonged disruption.

Expected Evidence / Criteria: BIA; dependency and failure-mode analysis; capacity/load evidence; DR architecture; exercise results with actual RTO/RPO and reconciliation; communication/escalation; deviations/CAPA; customer continuity inputs and recurring schedule.

Red Flags: Only tabletop exercise; no tenant/data reconciliation; actual RTO exceeds contract but reported as pass; hidden dependency not exercised; customer notifications delayed; CAPA absent.

content:

Expected Evidence / Criteria: Approved functional/design specifications; unique IDs and revision control; URS/risk-to-design bidirectional traceability; decision/comment log; interface/procedure allocations; test method and acceptance links; independent QA/SME approval; no unexplained orphan or many-to-one mappings.
Regulatory Alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(a), (k), 211.68; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§4.1, 4.4-4.7 and Annex 15 §§2-3; Guidance: ICH Q9(R1) §§3-5.

content:

content:

Follow-Up Probe: Calculate just below, at and above a decision boundary, then change an input or rule version and show how prior and recomputed outcomes remain distinguishable and reviewable.

content:

content:

Follow-Up Probe: Simulate two sites working offline while messages queue and a record is corrected in the source; show conflict resolution, chronology, duplicate prevention, approvals and QA-visible reconciliation evidence.

content:

Follow-Up Probe: Model stolen privileged credentials used to change clocks, configuration and records before exfiltration; identify exact preventive controls, correlated alerts, immutable evidence and affected-record query.

Red Flags: Encryption/key ownership vague; clocks independently editable; SIEM actor IDs cannot map to records; security logs retained too briefly; admin can alter evidence; incident design cannot query affected GxP data.

content:

Follow-Up Probe: Trace an emergency configuration fix from detection to production and retrospective review, then prove which exact baseline was active for records created before, during and after the change.

Red Flags: Configuration stored in uncontrolled workbook; production edited directly; environments share data/credentials; release manifest incomplete; rollback untested; records cannot identify applied baseline.

content:

Follow-Up Probe: Choose a control performed partly by supplier and customer and trace its complete data/evidence flow, monitoring threshold, failure escalation and fallback; identify any step assigned to neither party.

Red Flags: Sampling only completed tickets; termination timestamp later than observed activity; unmanaged local or vendor accounts; inherited entitlements omitted; service accounts still owned by leavers; no retrospective impact assessment for delayed removal.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-11-005]: Demonstrate how every non-human identity is inventoried, uniquely purposed, least-privileged, credential-managed, monitored, and assigned to a current accountable owner throughout operation.
Phase: Operations & Periodic Review | Domain: Access Management | Topic: Non-human and service accounts | Priority: High
Follow-Up Probe: Choose one high-privilege service account and show what prevents interactive use, credential sharing, unapproved secret extraction, and silent activity; then demonstrate the last credential rotation without disrupting or bypassing the validated process.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Service-account inventory, purpose and owner, entitlement mapping, vault records, rotation history, interactive-login restrictions, activity logs and alerts, dependency mapping, and exception approvals. Acceptance requires no orphaned identities, controlled secrets, attributable use, least privilege, and tested rotation or revocation.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 12.1 to 12.4; 21 CFR 11.10(d), 11.10(g), and 11.300 where Part 11 applies; NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 controls AC-2 and IA-5 as security guidance.
Red Flags: Unknown owner or purpose; shared credential in code or tickets; interactive login permitted without justification; no rotation; account activity outside expected jobs; inventory reconstructed manually for the audit.

metadata.expected_evidence: Service-account inventory, purpose and owner, entitlement mapping, vault records, rotation history, interactive-login restrictions, activity logs and alerts, dependency mapping, and exception approvals. Acceptance requires no orphaned identities, controlled secrets, attributable use, least privilege
metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 12.1 to 12.4; 21 CFR 11.10(d), 11.10(g), and 11.300 where Part 11 applies; NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 controls AC-2 and IA-5 as security guidance.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-11-006]: Using an auditor-selected GxP record, demonstrate how audit-trail review identifies, evaluates, and resolves every material creation, modification, deletion, reprocessing, status change, and security event relevant to the quality decision.
Phase: Operations & Periodic Review | Domain: Audit Trail | Topic: Risk-based audit-trail review | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Show the complete event population for the same record directly from the system, including events not displayed in the routine review report, and explain how reviewers detect missing periods, disabled logging, administrator activity, clock differences, or repeated attempts that did not change the final value.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Audit-trail configuration and risk assessment, review procedure and frequency, raw system-generated event export, reviewer record, linked source record, exception investigation, reviewer training, and periodic verification of audit-trail availability. Acceptance requires complete intelligible events, independent and timely review, documented reasons for GxP changes, and traceable resolution before the associated decision where required.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 9 and 12.4; 21 CFR 11.10(e); FDA Data Integrity and Compliance With Drug CGMP Q&A; PIC/S PI 041-1.
Red Flags: Audit trail disabled, configurable by conflicted users, incomplete, unintelligible, or unavailable; review limited to final values; missing reasons; unexplained gaps; late review after batch or quality decision; admin actions excluded.

metadata.expected_evidence: Audit-trail configuration and risk assessment, review procedure and frequency, raw system-generated event export, reviewer record, linked source record, exception investigation, reviewer training, and periodic verification of audit-trail availability. Acceptance requires complete intelligible events
metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 9 and 12.4; 21 CFR 11.10(e); FDA Data Integrity and Compliance With Drug CGMP Q&A; PIC/S PI 041-1.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-11-007]: Select a completed electronic signature and prove from the live record and underlying controls that the signer identity, date and time, signature meaning, credential use, and permanent linkage to the exact signed record version remain unambiguous and non-transferable.
Phase: Operations & Periodic Review | Domain: Electronic Signatures | Topic: Signature meaning and record linkage | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Demonstrate what happens when the signed record is subsequently corrected, migrated, exported, or archived, and show that the signature cannot be excised, copied to another record, or displayed against a changed version without an attributable event.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Signed record, signature manifestation, identity record, authentication configuration, signature and audit logs, record-version history, signature policy, and migration or archive test where relevant. Acceptance requires unique signer control, recorded name/date/time/meaning, permanent linkage, preservation after record lifecycle events, and no shared credentials.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 14; 21 CFR 11.50, 11.70, 11.100, 11.200, and 11.300 where Part 11 applies.
Red Flags: Signature not tied to a record version; missing meaning or timestamp; shared credentials; signature can be copied or detached; correction changes signed content without new signature; archive or export loses linkage.

metadata.expected_evidence: Signed record, signature manifestation, identity record, authentication configuration, signature and audit logs, record-version history, signature policy, and migration or archive test where relevant. Acceptance requires unique signer control, recorded name/date/time/meaning, permanent linkage, pres
metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 14; 21 CFR 11.50, 11.70, 11.100, 11.200, and 11.300 where Part 11 applies.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-11-008]: Retrieve an auditor-selected record from the oldest active retention cohort and demonstrate that its content, context, critical metadata, audit trail, and associated signatures remain accurate, readable, intelligible, and available for review without relying on undocumented expert intervention.
Phase: Operations & Periodic Review | Domain: Data Integrity | Topic: Retention-period accessibility and readability | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Repeat the retrieval for a record created before the latest major application, database, operating-system, or viewer change and explain how continued readability and meaning were verified when technology changed.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Retention schedule, record inventory, storage and archive architecture, retrieval procedure, periodic readability and integrity checks, sample record with metadata and audit trail, and technology-change impact assessments. Acceptance requires timely retrieval, complete content and context, verified integrity, controlled access, and documented remediation of failed checks.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7.1 and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(b) and 11.10(c) where Part 11 applies; applicable predicate-rule retention requirements.
Red Flags: Old records cannot be retrieved promptly; proprietary viewer unavailable; metadata or audit trail omitted; integrity checks never performed; retention period guessed; technology changes not assessed; reliance on an unsupported production environment.

metadata.expected_evidence: Retention schedule, record inventory, storage and archive architecture, retrieval procedure, periodic readability and integrity checks, sample record with metadata and audit trail, and technology-change impact assessments. Acceptance requires timely retrieval, complete content and context, verified
metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7.1 and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(b) and 11.10(c) where Part 11 applies; applicable predicate-rule retention requirements.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-11-009]: Reconcile the approved inventory of GxP data, metadata, audit trails, configurations, encryption material, and supporting components to the live backup job definitions and demonstrate that the backup scope remains complete after system changes.
Phase: Operations & Periodic Review | Domain: Backup & Disaster Recovery | Topic: Backup population completeness | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Select one newly added or changed component and one apparently successful backup; prove that the required content was actually captured and usable rather than merely that the job ended with a success status.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Data and component inventory, backup architecture and job definitions, retention and immutability settings, job and exception logs, scope reconciliation, change records, and content verification. Acceptance requires complete risk-based scope, monitored failures, protected copies, periodic reconciliation after change, and no unapproved exclusions.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 7.2; 21 CFR 211.68(b); 21 CFR 11.10(c) where Part 11 applies; NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 control CP-9 as security guidance.
Red Flags: Scope cannot be reconciled; successful status accepted without content verification; audit trails, attachments, or keys excluded; backup changes outside change control; failed jobs aged or suppressed; no protected off-system copy where risk requires it.

metadata.expected_evidence: Data and component inventory, backup architecture and job definitions, retention and immutability settings, job and exception logs, scope reconciliation, change records, and content verification. Acceptance requires complete risk-based scope, monitored failures, protected copies, periodic reconcilia
metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 7.2; 21 CFR 211.68(b); 21 CFR 11.10(c) where Part 11 applies; NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 control CP-9 as security guidance.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-11-010]: Reperform the evidence chain for the last recovery exercise and show that the recovered service met approved recovery time and recovery point objectives while preserving record completeness, data meaning, audit trails, interfaces, security, and business-process usability.
Phase: Operations & Periodic Review | Domain: Business Continuity | Topic: Restore and recovery effectiveness | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Show the last failed or partially successful restore step, how the failure was detected, what data interval or functionality was at risk, and whether the retest proved the corrective action rather than repeating only the successful path.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Approved recovery plan, business impact analysis, RTO and RPO, exercise protocol and raw timestamps, restored-data reconciliation, security and interface checks, business and Quality acceptance, deviations, CAPA, and retest. Acceptance requires objectives achieved or deviations formally assessed with effective remediation and no unexplained data loss.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7.2 and 16; 21 CFR 211.68(b); NIST SP 800-34 Rev. 1 and NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 CP controls as nonbinding guidance.
Red Flags: Restore never tested; test excludes audit trails, interfaces, keys, or business verification; RTO or RPO missed without risk acceptance; failed step omitted; recovered data not reconciled; exercise performed only on unlike infrastructure.

metadata.expected_evidence: Approved recovery plan, business impact analysis, RTO and RPO, exercise protocol and raw timestamps, restored-data reconciliation, security and interface checks, business and Quality acceptance, deviations, CAPA, and retest. metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7.2 and 16; 21 CFR 211.68(b); NIST SP 800-34 Rev. 1 and NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 CP controls as nonbinding guidance.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-11-011]: Trace a complete GxP data transfer from authoritative source through middleware to target and downstream report, demonstrating how completeness, accuracy, sequence, attribution, timestamps, and processing status are reconciled in routine operation.
Phase: Operations & Periodic Review | Domain: Interfaces & Integrations | Topic: Operational reconciliation of data transfers | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Use the last failed, duplicate, delayed, partial, or out-of-order transfer and show how the system prevented silent loss or double processing, preserved the original event, controlled reprocessing, and assessed downstream quality impact.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Interface inventory and data mapping, control totals or acknowledgements, queue and transaction logs, error and retry configuration, reconciliation reports, incident or deviation, reprocessing record, and downstream verification. Acceptance requires end-to-end traceability, controlled error handling, no silent loss or duplication, and documented impact assessment.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 5, 7, 8, 9, and 13; 21 CFR 11.10(a), 11.10(e), 11.10(f), and 11.10(h) where Part 11 applies.
Red Flags: No end-to-end identifier or reconciliation; monitoring only transport availability; discarded error messages; uncontrolled replay; duplicate processing; manual correction outside audit trail; source and target totals disagree without investigation.

metadata.expected_evidence: Interface inventory and data mapping, control totals or acknowledgements, queue and transaction logs, error and retry configuration, reconciliation reports, incident or deviation, reprocessing record, and downstream verification. document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-11-012]: Starting from the full alert population, demonstrate how quality-relevant alarms are rationalized, prioritized, routed, acknowledged, investigated, and closed within defined limits, including periods when the primary responder is unavailable.
Phase: Operations & Periodic Review | Domain: Operations Monitoring | Topic: Alarm and alert response | Priority: High
Follow-Up Probe: Select one suppressed, auto-closed, repeated, or missed alert and reconstruct what occurred in the regulated process during the blind period; explain how the impact population was identified and why recurrence is controlled.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Alert catalogue and rationale, thresholds, routing and escalation rules, on-call coverage, raw alert history, acknowledgement and response records, suppression approvals, deviations or incidents, trend review, and effectiveness actions. Acceptance requires complete population visibility, risk-based response limits, controlled suppression, and impact assessment for missed alerts.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 1, 11, and 13; 21 CFR 211.68(a); ICH Q9(R1) Sections 3 and 4.
Red Flags: No complete alert population; alert floods or chronic recurrence; critical alert auto-closed; undocumented suppression; response SLA measured without quality impact; blind periods not assessed; no escalation outside business hours.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-11-013]: Show how the periodic evaluation derives and challenges incident, deviation, problem, and service-request trends from complete source populations rather than relying on ticket labels or manually selected quality events.
Phase: Operations & Periodic Review | Domain: Incident & Deviation Management | Topic: Operational event trend inclusion | Priority: High
Follow-Up Probe: Reclassify a sample of low-severity or non-GxP-labelled tickets against the system's intended use and data flows; explain any event that should have triggered a deviation, validation impact assessment, or broader retrospective review.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Incident and deviation taxonomy, linkage rules, complete ITSM and quality-event extracts, trend method, reclassification controls, management review, and actions. Acceptance requires reconciled populations, documented inclusion and exclusion logic, challenge of repeat events, and escalation of potential GxP impact.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 11 and 13; ICH Q9(R1) Section 4; PIC/S PI 041-1 Sections 6 and 9.
Red Flags: IT and Quality populations do not reconcile; GxP impact determined by service-desk category alone; recurring events fragmented; exclusions lack rationale; data corrections treated as requests rather than events; trend omits supplier cases.

metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 11 and 13; ICH Q9(R1) Section 4; PIC/S PI 041-1 Sections 6 and 9.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-11-014]: For the highest-risk recurring problem, demonstrate that root cause and CAPA effectiveness were established with objective evidence and that recurrence was assessed across related systems, sites, records, and supplier services.
Phase: Operations & Periodic Review | Domain: Problem & CAPA Management | Topic: Recurrence and CAPA effectiveness | Priority: High
Follow-Up Probe: Show the search logic used to declare no recurrence, then broaden it to synonyms, different ticket categories, similar error codes, manual corrections, and near misses; explain any events the original effectiveness check missed.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Problem investigation, causal evidence, CAPA plan, implementation records, cross-system applicability assessment, defined effectiveness measure and observation period, complete recurrence query, results, and Quality approval. Acceptance requires cause-specific measures, adequate time and population, no unexplained recurrence, and escalation when effectiveness is not demonstrated.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 11 and 13; ICH Q9(R1) Sections 4.4 and 4.6; PIC/S PI 041-1 Sections 6 and 9.
Red Flags: Root cause stated as human error without systemic analysis; CAPA effectiveness equals task completion; recurrence query undocumented or narrow; repeat events relabelled; no cross-system assessment; failed effectiveness check not reopened.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-11-015]: Using the complete change and release history since the previous evaluation, demonstrate how cumulative effects on intended use, data integrity, security, performance, interfaces, supplier dependencies, and validation status were assessed.

Expected Evidence / Criteria: Complete change population, releases and supplier changes, affected-component mapping, cumulative-impact method, revised risk and traceability records, regression evidence, periodic-evaluation conclusion, and Quality approvals. Acceptance requires reconciliation to deployment and configuration history and explicit assessment of repeated changes to critical functions.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.2, 10, and 11; 21 CFR 11.10(a) and 11.10(k); 21 CFR 211.68(b); ICH Q9(R1) Section 4.6.
Red Flags: Deployment population exceeds approved changes; minor changes never aggregated; repeated changes to same control; supplier releases omitted; incidents rise after changes; validation documents and system description not updated.

metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.2, 10, and 11; 21 CFR 11.10(a) and 11.10(k); 21 CFR 211.68(b); ICH Q9(R1) Section 4.6.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-11-016]: Compare the live production configuration to the approved baseline and demonstrate how authorized differences, temporary settings, feature flags, emergency changes, and supplier-managed parameters are detected and governed.
Phase: Operations & Periodic Review | Domain: Configuration Management | Topic: Production configuration drift | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: The auditor will select a security, audit-trail, retention, calculation, interface, or workflow parameter from the live system and ask for its last change, approver, test evidence, and current baseline entry.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Approved baseline, automated or controlled configuration export, comparison report, parameter ownership, authorized change records, temporary-change expiry, drift alerts, investigation, and re-baselining approval. Acceptance requires complete critical-parameter coverage and no unexplained production difference.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.3, 10, and 11; 21 CFR 211.68(b); 21 CFR 11.10(k) where Part 11 applies.
Red Flags: No approved baseline; comparison omits critical parameters; manual snapshots without provenance; unexplained drift; expired feature flags; supplier settings inaccessible; direct changes visible only in audit logs after the fact.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-11-017]: Trace the vulnerability population for the system to patch, mitigation, acceptance, or retirement decisions and demonstrate how product quality, data integrity, availability, exploitability, supplier constraints, and validation impact determine remediation priority.
Phase: Operations & Periodic Review | Domain: Cybersecurity | Topic: Vulnerability and patch risk decisions | Priority: Critical

Expected Evidence / Criteria: Asset and software inventory, scanner and supplier advisories, vulnerability records, applicability validation, risk decisions, patch changes and tests, compensating controls and logs, exception expiry, and periodic review. Acceptance requires complete scope, timely risk-based action, approved and time-bound exceptions, and verified compensating controls.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 1, 11, and 12; NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 and NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 SI and RA controls as nonbinding security guidance.
Red Flags: Assets missing from scan scope; risk accepted from CVSS alone; overdue critical vulnerabilities; compensating control asserted without telemetry; exception has no expiry; supplier constraint accepted indefinitely; patch not linked to validation impact.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-11-018]: Demonstrate that security logging covers the events capable of affecting regulated data or validated configuration and that detections remain effective when logs are delayed, malformed, tampered with, or unavailable.

Acceptance requires coverage of critical events, protected and synchronized logs, tested detections, monitored collection failures, and retained evidence.

Red Flags: Critical log sources not onboarded; clocks not synchronized; administrators can alter logs; collection gaps invisible; alert never tested; retention shorter than record or investigation need; security events not assessed for GxP impact.

metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 9, 12, and 13; 21 CFR 11.10(e) where Part 11 applies; NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 Detect and Respond functions as nonbinding guidance.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-11-019]: For one critical provider-managed control, demonstrate how the regulated company obtains sufficient ongoing assurance from contract obligations, service evidence, performance data, exceptions, and independent verification rather than relying solely on a certification.

Red Flags: Certification treated as complete evidence; expired bridge period; agreement omits GxP records or inspection access; supplier changes not notified; subprocessor unknown; exceptions not assessed; responsibility gap for backup, logs, incidents, or data return.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-11-020]: Demonstrate how capacity, response time, job completion, error rate, queue depth, storage growth, and availability trends are converted into risk-based actions before degraded service affects data completeness or regulated decisions.
Phase: Operations & Periodic Review | Domain: Performance & Reliability | Topic: Capacity and reliability trends | Priority: High

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-11-021]: For each role capable of creating, reviewing, administering, changing, recovering, or investigating GxP records, demonstrate that current procedures and task-specific competence were effective before the person performed unsupervised work.

Red Flags: Access granted before training; training only attendance-based; obsolete procedure; vendor personnel omitted; deviation reveals procedure-content gap; recurring retraining without system or process correction; no competency evidence for critical tasks.

Follow-Up Probe: Compare the supplier's final report with your own telemetry and affected-record analysis, identify inconsistencies or missing evidence, and show how your organization challenged conclusions rather than accepting provider closure.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Quality or service agreement, notification timestamps, joint timeline, provider and customer logs, shared-responsibility matrix, impact assessment, supplier root cause and CAPA, internal challenge, SLA remedies, subprocessor evidence, and Quality closure. Acceptance requires timely access, reconciled facts, and effective actions under retained user accountability.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 3, 7, 12, 13, and 16; NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 3 as nonbinding incident-response guidance.
Red Flags: Supplier notified late; evidence withheld; internal assessment relies only on provider summary; subprocessor unknown; tenant data not reconciled; CAPA acceptance unchallenged; contract lacks incident or inspection evidence obligations.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-13-012]: Demonstrate how the investigation distinguished root cause, contributing causes, detection-control failure, and organizational or process conditions using evidence that can reproduce and explain the observed event.
Phase: Incident, Problem & Deviation Management | Domain: Problem Management | Topic: Evidence-based root cause | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Present the strongest competing causal hypothesis, show the discriminating evidence used to reject it, and explain which facts remain uncertain and how that uncertainty changes corrective action or monitoring.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Problem statement, complete timeline, evidence catalogue, technical and process analysis, hypotheses, experiments or reproduction, causal chain, contributing factors, detection failure, uncertainty, cross-functional review, and approved conclusion. Acceptance requires evidence sufficient to explain occurrence and recurrence and actions addressing the causal mechanism.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 13; ICH Q9(R1) Sections 4.2, 4.3, and 5; PIC/S PI 041-1 Sections 6 and 9.
Red Flags: Root cause is 'human error,' 'software glitch,' or 'network issue' without causal evidence; competing hypotheses absent; event not reproducible or bounded; detection failure ignored; uncertainty concealed; supplier statement accepted verbatim.

metadata.expected_evidence: Problem statement, complete timeline, evidence catalogue, technical and process analysis, hypotheses, experiments or reproduction, causal chain, contributing factors, detection failure, uncertainty, cross-functional review, and approved conclusion. Acceptance requires evidence sufficient to explain

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-13-013]: Show how the investigation searched for recurrence and analogous failure across alternate error codes, ticket categories, sites, versions, interfaces, manual corrections, supplier services, and near misses.
Phase: Incident, Problem & Deviation Management | Domain: Problem Management | Topic: Recurrence and similar-event search | Priority: High
Follow-Up Probe: Rerun the search using broader technical and business synonyms and compare the newly found population with the one used to conclude that the event was isolated.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Documented search strategy, systems and time window, query terms and logic, results, clustering method, applicability decisions, historical impact review, and CAPA scope. Acceptance requires reproducible, sufficiently broad search and escalation when similar events are identified.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 11 and 13; ICH Q9(R1) Sections 4.3 and 4.6; PIC/S PI 041-1 Sections 6 and 9.
Red Flags: Search limited to exact error code or same system; query not retained; low-severity and supplier cases excluded; similar events relabelled; historical product or data impact not revisited; systemic pattern declared isolated.

metadata.expected_evidence: Documented search strategy, systems and time window, query terms and logic, results, clustering method, applicability decisions, historical impact review, and CAPA scope. Acceptance requires reproducible, sufficiently broad search and escalation when similar events are identified.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-13-014]: For an event attributed to human error, demonstrate how system design, workload, procedure clarity, training effectiveness, access, interface usability, supervision, incentives, and error-detection controls were evaluated as causal or contributing conditions.
Phase: Incident, Problem & Deviation Management | Domain: Human Factors & Quality Culture | Topic: Human-error causal challenge | Priority: High
Follow-Up Probe: Place a competent person unfamiliar with the event in the same controlled scenario and show whether the process and system reliably lead to the correct action without relying on memory or informal knowledge.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Task analysis, procedure and training content, competence, workload and environment, access and UI controls, system checks, supervision, interviews, recurrence data, and redesigned controls. Acceptance requires systemic assessment and CAPA beyond retraining where the process permits predictable error.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 1, 2, 6, 12, and 13; 21 CFR 11.10(f), 11.10(g), and 11.10(i); PIC/S PI 041-1 Section 6.
Red Flags: Root cause ends at operator mistake; CAPA is retraining only; procedure ambiguous; system permits invalid sequence; workload or incentives ignored; same error recurs; punitive response discourages reporting. Finding trigger: evidence is missing, unapproved, incomplete, inconsistent, or cannot be reproduced for the auditor-selected sample.

metadata.expected_evidence: Task analysis, procedure and training content, competence, workload and environment, access and UI controls, system checks, supervision, interviews, recurrence data, and redesigned controls. Acceptance requires systemic assessment and CAPA beyond retraining where the process permits predictable erro

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-13-015]: Trace the incident backward through all changes and releases within the credible causal window and demonstrate how the implemented state differed from the tested and approved state.
Phase: Incident, Problem & Deviation Management | Domain: Change Management | Topic: Change-induced incident trace | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Include individually low-risk, emergency, infrastructure, feature-flag, supplier, and direct configuration changes, then explain why any temporal or technical correlation was excluded as a cause.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Causal-window rationale, complete deployment and configuration population, pre/post baselines, repository and supplier history, test evidence, incident timeline, correlation analysis, and change-process CAPA. Acceptance requires reconciliation to production sources and reassessment of affected change controls.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.2, 10, 11, and 13; 21 CFR 11.10(k); 21 CFR 211.68(b).
Red Flags: Change search limited to application tickets; feature flags or supplier releases omitted; approved and live baselines differ; correlation dismissed without analysis; testing gap not fed back to change process.

Acceptance requires reconciliation to production sources and reassessment of affected chang

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-13-016]: Establish a defensible common timeline across application, database, operating system, identity, interface, cloud, monitoring, supplier, and quality records, accounting for time zones, daylight-saving changes, clock drift, latency, and log buffering.
Phase: Incident, Problem & Deviation Management | Domain: Forensic Traceability | Topic: Timestamp and log correlation | Priority: High
Follow-Up Probe: Select two events whose apparent order changes after normalization and show which chronology is authoritative, how uncertainty was bounded, and whether the revised sequence changes root cause or affected population.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Time-source architecture, synchronization and drift monitoring, time-zone and daylight-saving rules, raw logs with source metadata, normalization method, latency estimates, common timeline, and uncertainty. Acceptance requires reproducible conversion and causal conclusions robust to known timing error.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 9, 12.4, and 13; 21 CFR 11.10(e); MHRA GxP Data Integrity Guidance Section 5.1 as nonbinding guidance.
Red Flags: Timeline mixes local and UTC without conversion; clock drift unknown; screenshots replace raw logs; buffered events treated as occurrence time; event order uncertain but stated as fact; no impact on causal conclusion assessed.

metadata.expected_evidence: Time-source architecture, synchronization and drift monitoring, time-zone and daylight-saving rules, raw logs with source metadata, normalization method, latency estimates, common timeline, and uncertainty. Acceptance requires reproducible conversion and causal conclusions robust to known timing err

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-13-017]: Demonstrate that each interim workaround or compensating control is specific to the identified failure mode, effective for the full affected population, sustainable across shifts and sites, monitored, and time-bound until permanent correction.
Phase: Incident, Problem & Deviation Management | Domain: Interim Risk Control | Topic: Workaround and compensating-control effectiveness | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Observe or simulate the workaround under peak workload and staff absence, then show how missed execution, transcription error, duplicate processing, or workaround drift is independently detected.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Interim-control design, risk assessment, instructions, training, staffing and capacity, control execution records, independent verification, monitoring, deviations, expiry and escalation, and permanent-fix plan. Acceptance requires verified effectiveness and no uncontrolled extension.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 1, 13, and 16; ICH Q9(R1) Sections 4.4 to 4.6; PIC/S PI 041-1 Sections 6 and 9.
Red Flags: Workaround relies on memory; no capacity analysis; execution records incomplete; extension automatic; missed steps not detected; control owner conflicted; permanent fix repeatedly deferred; workaround changes GxP data outside audit trail.

metadata.expected_evidence: Interim-control design, risk assessment, instructions, training, staffing and capacity, control execution records, independent verification, monitoring, deviations, expiry and escalation, and permanent-fix plan. Acceptance requires verified effectiveness and no uncontrolled extension.
metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 1, 13, and 16; ICH Q9(R1) Sections 4.4 to 4.6; PIC/S PI 041-1 Sections 6 and 9.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-13-018]: Trace one corrected or recovered record from original state through authorization, preserved source evidence, correction or replay method, independent verification, audit trail, downstream reconciliation, and final quality disposition.
Phase: Incident, Problem & Deviation Management | Domain: Data Correction & Recovery | Topic: Controlled repair of affected records | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Demonstrate how the process prevents selective correction, overwriting of the original, duplicate downstream use, and correction by a person who performed or benefits from the original action.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Affected-record population, approved correction protocol, preserved originals, authorized tools and identities, before and after values, reasons, audit trails, validation or verification of scripts, independent checks, downstream reconciliation, and Quality approval. Acceptance requires complete traceability and no loss of original evidence.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 5, 6, 7, 9, and 13; 21 CFR 11.10(a) and 11.10(e); FDA Data Integrity Q&A; PIC/S PI 041-1.
Red Flags: Original overwritten; correction script untested; bulk population not reconciled; selective records repaired; conflicted person approves; audit trail reason missing; downstream reports or decisions not refreshed; backup copy treated as original without verification.

metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 5, 6, 7, 9, and 13; 21 CFR 11.10(a) and 11.10(e); FDA Data Integrity Q&A; PIC/S PI 041-1.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-13-019]: Demonstrate bidirectional linkage among the technical incident, quality deviation, affected records or batches, investigation, changes, CAPA, and disposition so that no part of the evidence or decision can be closed independently.
Phase: Incident, Problem & Deviation Management | Domain: Quality Event Integration | Topic: Incident-deviation-batch linkage | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Select one linked item closed earlier than another and explain how new facts propagated to all dependent decisions, including any released batch, approved record, or previously accepted residual risk.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Cross-system linkage procedure and identifiers, synchronized scope and timelines, affected batch or record list, shared evidence, change and CAPA references, decision updates, closure dependencies, and Quality oversight. Acceptance requires consistent facts and controlled propagation of material updates.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.2 and 13; 21 CFR 211.192 where applicable; ICH Q9(R1) Section 4.6.
Red Flags: IT and Quality scopes differ; no common identifier; one record closes while material actions remain open; batch or record list inconsistent; new root-cause evidence not propagated; supplier ticket absent from deviation.

content:

Phase: Incident, Problem & Deviation Management | Domain: CAPA Management | Topic: Cause-to-action traceability | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Remove the proposed training and procedure actions from the plan and show which technical, process, governance, or supplier control prevents recurrence; explain any causal factor left without an action.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Approved causal analysis, cause-to-CAPA map, action design and owner, risk priority, interim controls, technical and process implementation, cross-system applicability, validation or change records, due dates, and Quality approval. Acceptance requires full causal coverage and proportionate preventive action.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 13; ICH Q9(R1) Sections 4.4 to 4.6; PIC/S PI 041-1 Sections 6 and 9.
Red Flags: CAPA consists only of retraining or SOP revision; root cause has no corresponding action; detection failure ignored; supplier cause not governed; applicability limited without rationale; due dates repeatedly extended.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-13-021]: Demonstrate that CAPA effectiveness was measured over a population and period capable of revealing recurrence, and that both the corrected control and the detection control operated successfully under representative and adverse conditions.
Phase: Incident, Problem & Deviation Management | Domain: CAPA Effectiveness | Topic: Sustained effectiveness verification | Priority: High
Follow-Up Probe: Rerun the documented effectiveness query against current incident, deviation, monitoring, audit-trail exception, change, and supplier data and explain any near miss, workaround, or differently classified recurrence.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Predefined effectiveness criteria, baseline, population, observation period, source query, adverse-condition or control test, results, independent review, recurrence assessment, and response to failure. Acceptance requires cause-specific measures, sufficient opportunity for recurrence, and reopening or escalation when criteria are unmet.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 11 and 13; ICH Q9(R1) Section 4.6; PIC/S PI 041-1 Sections 6 and 9.
Red Flags: Effectiveness equals completion; observation period too short; query exact-match only; near misses excluded; source data incomplete; check performed by action owner without independent review; failed result not reopened.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-13-024]: Demonstrate that closure reflects resolved containment, bounded impact, supported root cause, implemented or governed CAPA, reconciled records, restored validated state, and explicitly accepted residual risk.
Phase: Incident, Problem & Deviation Management | Domain: Incident Closure Governance | Topic: Evidence-based closure and residual risk | Priority: Critical

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-14-001]: Reconstruct the approved retirement decision and demonstrate how business, Quality, records, security, privacy, legal, supplier, continuity, and technical owners agreed the system boundary, timing, successor capability, retained obligations, and exit criteria.
Phase: Decommissioning, Data Retention & Migration | Domain: Decommissioning Governance | Topic: Retirement decision and scope | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Identify the strongest dependency or regulated use arguing against shutdown and show the objective evidence that it was replaced, archived, risk-controlled, or formally accepted before the final irreversible step.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Approved retirement business case, GxP and regulatory assessment, scope and dependency analysis, accountable owners, successor and archive decisions, risk assessment, legal and retention review, exit criteria, timeline, and Quality approval. Acceptance requires complete scope, no unresolved critical dependency, and explicit control of retained obligations.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 lifecycle principle and Sections 1, 4.3, 7, 16, and 17; ICH Q9(R1) Sections 3 and 4.
Red Flags: Retirement approved by project or IT alone; scope differs from live inventory; open deviations, legal holds, or regulated uses omitted; exit criteria vague; irreversible shutdown scheduled before evidence completion; Quality approval absent.

GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-14-005]: Trace archive requirements for accessibility, readability, integrity, authenticity, security, metadata, audit trails, signatures, search, copies, retention, and destruction into the approved archive design and operating controls.
Phase: Decommissioning, Data Retention & Migration | Domain: Archiving | Topic: Archive requirements and design | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Demonstrate how the archive remains usable if the original application, database, vendor, license server, identity provider, encryption algorithm, or viewer no longer exists.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Archive URS or requirements, risk assessment, data and metadata model, format and viewer strategy, security and access design, integrity checks, search and copy capability, retention and legal-hold controls, backup and recovery, technology-refresh plan, and approvals. Acceptance requires long-term usability independent of unsupported production components.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7, 8, 9, 14, and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(b) and 11.10(c) where Part 11 applies.
Red Flags: Archive is only file storage; proprietary viewer dependency unaddressed; audit trails or signatures excluded; no integrity monitoring; original identity context lost; retention and deletion manual; archive recovery absent.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-14-006]: Demonstrate how migration scope, sequencing, freeze periods, coexistence, transformation, reconciliation, exception handling, rollback, source preservation, and final cutover were derived from data and process risk.
Phase: Decommissioning, Data Retention & Migration | Domain: Data Migration | Topic: Migration strategy and risk | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Assume the source must be shut down after a partially successful migration and explain how rejected records, late transactions, interfaces, manual workarounds, and rollback or forward recovery remain controlled without creating two conflicting systems of record.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Approved migration plan and risk assessment, source and target scopes, freeze and cutover design, data ownership, transformation rules, validation strategy, reconciliation, reject handling, rollback or forward-fix plan, source preservation, responsibilities, and Quality approval. Acceptance requires one authoritative record at each point and controlled exception paths.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.8, 5, 7, 9, 10, and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(a) to 11.10(c) and 11.10(e) where Part 11 applies; ICH Q9(R1) Section 4.
Red Flags: No authoritative-system rule during coexistence; late transactions omitted; rejects handled informally; rollback ignores new records; source altered or destroyed before acceptance; migration risk generic; Quality not involved.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-14-007]: Trace every transformation of critical data and metadata from source representation to target and demonstrate that value, precision, units, code meaning, relationships, null semantics, status, chronology, and attribution remain unchanged or are explicitly approved.
Phase: Decommissioning, Data Retention & Migration | Domain: Data Migration | Topic: Mapping and preservation of meaning | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Select one defaulted, concatenated, split, rounded, truncated, recoded, unmapped, or deprecated value and show how its original meaning and downstream use can still be reconstructed.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Source and target dictionaries, approved mapping, transformation specifications, code and unit crosswalks, precision rules, relationship handling, scripts under control, test evidence, exceptions, and business or Quality sign-off. Acceptance requires no unapproved change of value or meaning and retained provenance for approved transformations.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 4.8; 21 CFR 11.10(a) and 11.10(b); PIC/S PI 041-1 data-lifecycle principles.
Red Flags: Mapping inferred from code; unit or precision changes undocumented; nulls converted to zero; obsolete codes dropped; relationship broken; transformation script differs from approved version; downstream report not reconciled.

metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 4.8; 21 CFR 11.10(a) and 11.10(b); PIC/S PI 041-1 data-lifecycle principles.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-14-008]: Reconcile the full source population to extracted, transformed, loaded, rejected, quarantined, duplicated, and excluded populations using immutable cut-off criteria and independent control totals.
Phase: Decommissioning, Data Retention & Migration | Domain: Data Migration | Topic: Population and control-total reconciliation | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Explain how matching total row counts could still hide missing child records, duplicated parents, changed amounts, null fields, attachment loss, or status shifts and show the additional checks that reveal each risk.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Frozen source population, extraction logs, staged and target counts, field totals, relational counts, hash or checksum evidence where appropriate, reject and exclusion logs, duplicate checks, attachments and audit-trail totals, independent review, and approved reconciliation. Acceptance requires every source item accounted for exactly once or formally dispositioned.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.8 and 7; 21 CFR 11.10(a) to 11.10(c); FDA Data Integrity Q&A.
Red Flags: Only row count used; source not frozen; excludes and rejects netted out; child or attachment counts absent; duplicate detection weak; reconciliation prepared by migration developer only; unexplained variance accepted.

metadata.expected_evidence: Frozen source population, extraction logs, staged and target counts, field totals, relational counts, hash or checksum evidence where appropriate, reject and exclusion logs, duplicate checks, attachments and audit-trail totals, independent review, and approved reconciliation.
