metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.8 and 7; 21 CFR 11.10(a) to 11.10(c); FDA Data Integrity Q&A.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-14-009]: For an auditor-selected critical record, trace the complete source-to-target chain and prove preservation of content, context, metadata, audit trail, signatures, attachments, calculations, relationships, and inspection copies.
Phase: Decommissioning, Data Retention & Migration | Domain: Data Integrity | Topic: Critical record source-to-target trace | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Select a corrected, signed, rejected, or reopened record with multiple versions and explain how the target distinguishes original, prior, current, and superseded states without flattening history.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Source record and native history, extract and transformation trace, target record and versions, metadata, audit trail, signature links, attachments, related records, calculation or report output, and copy. Acceptance requires field-level equivalence or approved transformation with complete provenance.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.8, 7, 8, 9, 14, and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(a) to 11.10(c), 11.10(e), 11.50, and 11.70.
Red Flags: History flattened; only current value migrated; attachments or links missing; signatures displayed without version; calculations differ; target copy omits context; sample chosen by migration team only.

metadata.expected_evidence: Source record and native history, extract and transformation trace, target record and versions, metadata, audit trail, signature links, attachments, related records, calculation or report output, and copy. Acceptance requires field-level equivalence or approved transformation with complete provenanc

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-14-010]: Demonstrate how every migration exception is uniquely identified, preserved, investigated, risk-assessed, corrected under control, independently verified, reprocessed once, and included in final reconciliation.
Phase: Decommissioning, Data Retention & Migration | Domain: Migration Exceptions | Topic: Rejected and quarantined records | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Select the oldest or repeatedly failed exception and show why it did not reveal a broader mapping or source-quality problem; search the accepted population for the same causal pattern.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Immutable exception log, original rejected payload, error and cause, affected-record and broader-scope assessment, controlled correction, approval, reprocessing logs, duplicate prevention, independent check, and final disposition. Acceptance requires zero unexplained exceptions at release and systemic action for recurring causes.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.2, 4.8, 7, 9, and 13; 21 CFR 11.10(a) and 11.10(e); ICH Q9(R1) Section 4.
Red Flags: Exception log mutable; original payload lost; manual fix unapproved; repeated errors treated individually; rejected records excluded from totals; reprocessing creates duplicates; open critical exceptions at shutdown.

metadata.expected_evidence: Immutable exception log, original rejected payload, error and cause, affected-record and broader-scope assessment, controlled correction, approval, reprocessing logs, duplicate prevention, independent check, and final disposition. Acceptance requires zero unexplained exceptions at release and system
metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.2, 4.8, 7, 9, and 13; 21 CFR 11.10(a) and 11.10(e); ICH Q9(R1) Section 4.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-14-011]: Demonstrate that the migration or archive preserves every required audit event, prior value, new value, actor, timestamp, action, reason, record linkage, and review status in an intelligible and reviewable form.
Phase: Decommissioning, Data Retention & Migration | Domain: Audit Trail | Topic: Audit-trail preservation | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Compare a raw source audit-trail export with the target or archive for events created by administrators, failed actions, deletions, configuration changes, and periods where user-facing reports normally filter events.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Source audit schema and configuration, full event population, mapping, transformation rules, target or archive events, intelligible display and electronic copy, event and record linkage, review capability, reconciliation, and access control. Acceptance requires complete history and no loss of meaning or reviewability.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 9 and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(e); FDA Data Integrity Q&A; PIC/S PI 041-1.
Red Flags: Only audit-trail PDF retained; prior values or reasons omitted; admin or failed events filtered; record linkage broken; timestamps transformed without trace; audit events not searchable or reviewable; source destroyed before reconciliation.

metadata.expected_evidence: Source audit schema and configuration, full event population, mapping, transformation rules, target or archive events, intelligible display and electronic copy, event and record linkage, review capability, reconciliation, and access control. Acceptance requires complete history and no loss of meanin
metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 9 and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(e); FDA Data Integrity Q&A; PIC/S PI 041-1.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-14-012]: Select a migrated or archived signed record and prove that signer identity, date and time, signature meaning, signed record version, and permanent linkage remain intact and cannot be reassigned or detached.
Phase: Decommissioning, Data Retention & Migration | Domain: Electronic Signatures | Topic: Signature linkage after migration | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Show how signer identity is resolved after the user account, directory, or original application has been removed and how later corrections or format conversions avoid making the original signature appear to approve changed content.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Source signed record and signature logs, identity reference, mapping, target or archive record version, manifestation, permanent linkage, correction behavior, copy output, and verification. Acceptance requires durable, unambiguous, non-transferable linkage independent of active user accounts.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 14 and 17; 21 CFR 11.50, 11.70, 11.100, and 11.200.
Red Flags: Signature preserved only as image or text; signer unresolved after account removal; version linkage lost; correction changes signed content without new signature; multiple signatures collapsed; export detaches signature. Finding trigger: evidence is missing, unapproved, incomplete, inconsistent, or cannot be reproduced for the auditor-selected sample.

metadata.expected_evidence: Source signed record and signature logs, identity reference, mapping, target or archive record version, manifestation, permanent linkage, correction behavior, copy output, and verification. Acceptance requires durable, unambiguous, non-transferable linkage independent of active user accounts.
metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 14 and 17; 21 CFR 11.50, 11.70, 11.100, and 11.200.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-14-013]: Demonstrate preservation of time-zone and clock context, attachments, images, file properties, external references, annotations, units, display rules, and paper-electronic relationships required to interpret each retained record.
Phase: Decommissioning, Data Retention & Migration | Domain: Metadata & Hybrid Records | Topic: Time, attachments, and contextual integrity | Priority: High
Follow-Up Probe: Select a record crossing a daylight-saving change or site time zone and one whose attachment has the same filename as another record; show unambiguous chronology, association, integrity, and retrieval.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Metadata inventory and mapping, time conversion rules, attachment identifiers and hashes where used, MIME and format handling, link and annotation mapping, hybrid-record index, test evidence, and reconciliation. Acceptance requires preserved association, meaning, chronology, and integrity.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.8, 7, 8, 9, and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(b), 11.10(c), and 11.10(e); MHRA GxP Data Integrity Guidance Section 5.1 as nonbinding guidance.
Red Flags: Timestamps normalized without original zone; attachments matched by filename only; links broken; unsupported files skipped; annotations omitted; paper-electronic index lost; duplicate files overwrite; hash or size not reconciled.

metadata.expected_evidence: Metadata inventory and mapping, time conversion rules, attachment identifiers and hashes where used, MIME and format handling, link and annotation mapping, hybrid-record index, test evidence, and reconciliation. Acceptance requires preserved association, meaning, chronology, and integrity.
metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.8, 7, 8, 9, and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(b), 11.10(c), and 11.10(e); MHRA GxP Data Integrity Guidance Section 5.1 as nonbinding guidance.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-14-014]: Reconstruct the cutover and prove which system was authoritative for each process, site, record class, and time interval, including how late transactions, backlogs, manual records, and interface queues were controlled.
Phase: Decommissioning, Data Retention & Migration | Domain: Cutover & Coexistence | Topic: Authoritative-system transition | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Select a record created near the cutover boundary and show how duplicate creation, update in the wrong system, clock difference, and delayed interface delivery were detected and reconciled.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Cutover plan, freeze and authority matrix, synchronized timeline, user and interface controls, queue and backlog inventory, communication, boundary reconciliation, duplicate checks, deviations, and acceptance. Acceptance requires one unambiguous authoritative record for every interval and resolved transition exceptions.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.8, 5, 7, 9, 10, and 16; 21 CFR 11.10(a), 11.10(e), and 11.10(f).
Red Flags: Authority rule unclear; both systems writable; boundary times differ; late queue omitted; user access not aligned to freeze; duplicate records; manual backlog unreconciled; source changed after final extract.

metadata.expected_evidence: Cutover plan, freeze and authority matrix, synchronized timeline, user and interface controls, queue and backlog inventory, communication, boundary reconciliation, duplicate checks, deviations, and acceptance. Acceptance requires one unambiguous authoritative record for every interval and resolved t
metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.8, 5, 7, 9, 10, and 16; 21 CFR 11.10(a), 11.10(e), and 11.10(f).

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-14-015]: Trace archive or migration risks and requirements to test scenarios, raw evidence, deviations, reconciliation, acceptance, and release, including boundary, negative, failure, recovery, and long-term retrieval cases.
Phase: Decommissioning, Data Retention & Migration | Domain: Validation / Assurance | Topic: Archive and migration verification | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Show the highest-risk requirement with reduced or no scripted testing and demonstrate why other objective evidence provides sufficient assurance; then present the last failed test and its full resolution chain.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Validation or assurance plan, risk and requirement trace, test strategy, controlled tools and environments, positive and negative tests, raw execution evidence, deviations and defects, reconciliation, retrieval and recovery tests, summary, and Quality approval. Acceptance requires assurance commensurate with risk and no unexplained failed requirement.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.1, 4.2, 4.7, 4.8, and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(a) where Part 11 applies; ICH Q9(R1) Section 3.
Red Flags: Testing focused on counts only; long-term retrieval omitted; failed test overwritten; automated tool unassessed; deviations open at release; traceability mechanical; excluded requirements unsupported; source destroyed before approval. Finding trigger: evidence is missing, unapproved, incomplete, inconsistent, or cannot be reproduced for the auditor-selected sample.

metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.1, 4.2, 4.7, 4.8, and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(a) where Part 11 applies; ICH Q9(R1) Section 3.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-14-016]: Retrieve an auditor-selected archived record without production-system access and demonstrate timely search, access, readability, integrity, intelligibility, audit history, signature linkage, and accurate human-readable and electronic copies.
Phase: Decommissioning, Data Retention & Migration | Domain: Archiving Operations | Topic: Retrieval, readability, and inspection copies | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Repeat the retrieval for the oldest cohort and for a record created before a major format, viewer, operating-system, or archive-platform change; explain every manual or specialist step required.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Archive search and retrieval procedure, access authorization, native or preserved representation, metadata and audit history, signature linkage, copies, integrity verification, retrieval SLA, platform-change tests, and exception handling. Acceptance requires reproducible timely retrieval with complete meaning and no dependence on the retired production environment.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7.1, 8, 9, 14, and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(b) and 11.10(c).
Red Flags: Retrieval requires retired application; oldest records unreadable; metadata or audit trail absent; signatures unresolved; electronic copy proprietary or incomplete; manual reconstruction undocumented; SLA missed without action.

metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7.1, 8, 9, 14, and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(b) and 11.10(c).

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-14-017]: Demonstrate how periodic checks prove archive accessibility, readability, integrity, security, backup, recovery, capacity, and viewer compatibility and how results trigger controlled technology refresh before records become at risk.
Phase: Decommissioning, Data Retention & Migration | Domain: Archiving Operations | Topic: Ongoing archive integrity and technology refresh | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Show the last failed integrity, retrieval, or compatibility check, identify every potentially affected object, and demonstrate correction, retrospective scope, retest, and trend action.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Periodic-check procedure and risk-based frequency, complete archive population, integrity and retrieval results, access and security reviews, backup and recovery tests, capacity and lifecycle monitoring, exceptions, remediation, refresh plan, and Quality review. Acceptance requires complete monitored coverage and effective response to failures.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7.1, 7.2, 11, 16, and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(c); NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 CP and SI controls as nonbinding guidance.
Red Flags: Only storage availability monitored; integrity check samples too narrow; failed object scope unknown; viewer lifecycle ignored; no restore test; archive exceptions aged; refresh occurs after support expiry; Quality not reviewing trends.

metadata.expected_evidence: Periodic-check procedure and risk-based frequency, complete archive population, integrity and retrieval results, access and security reviews, backup and recovery tests, capacity and lifecycle monitoring, exceptions, remediation, refresh plan, and Quality review. Acceptance requires complete monitore
metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7.1, 7.2, 11, 16, and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(c); NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 CP and SI controls as nonbinding guidance.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-14-018]: Demonstrate how post-retirement access is limited to current authorized roles, remains attributable, is periodically reviewed, and prevents alteration, bulk extraction, or administrator circumvention of retained GxP records.
Phase: Decommissioning, Data Retention & Migration | Domain: Access Management & Security | Topic: Post-retirement archive access | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Select one legacy administrator, former project member, vendor account, and service identity and prove termination or current justification across archive, storage, cloud, database, key vault, and backup layers.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Archive role design, named-user and service-account populations, approvals and reviews, leaver cleanup, privileged-access restrictions, immutable or write-protected controls, access and export logs, alerts, and exceptions. Acceptance requires least privilege, unique attribution, timely revocation, and independent monitoring.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7, 12, and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(c), 11.10(d), 11.10(e), and 11.10(g); GDPR Article 32 where personal data apply.
Red Flags: Project accounts remain; archive access not reviewed; shared administrator; write access unnecessary; exports unlogged; former supplier access active; lower storage or backup layer omitted; leaver process excludes archive.

metadata.expected_evidence: Archive role design, named-user and service-account populations, approvals and reviews, leaver cleanup, privileged-access restrictions, immutable or write-protected controls, access and export logs, alerts, and exceptions. metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7, 12, and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(c), 11.10(d), 11.10(e), and 11.10(g); GDPR Article 32 where personal data apply.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-14-019]: Demonstrate how encryption keys, signing certificates, trust chains, secrets, tokens, algorithms, and recovery material needed to access or verify retained records remain available, protected, attributable, and replaceable throughout retention.
Phase: Decommissioning, Data Retention & Migration | Domain: Cryptographic Lifecycle | Topic: Long-term keys, certificates, and secrets | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Simulate loss or expiry of the primary key or certificate and show the tested recovery, escrow, re-encryption, verification, and audit path without weakening access control or losing proof of historical signature validity.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Cryptographic dependency inventory, ownership, key and certificate lifecycle, escrow and backup, algorithm and expiry monitoring, recovery or re-encryption tests, access controls and logs, destruction rules, and technology-refresh plan. Acceptance requires tested continuity and no single undocumented key dependency.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7, 12, 16, and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(c) and 11.10(d); NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 SC and CP controls as nonbinding guidance.
Red Flags: Key owner unknown; single key copy; certificate expiry unmonitored; recovery untested; vendor key unavailable after contract; re-encryption changes provenance without control; destruction occurs before retention ends. Finding trigger: evidence is missing, unapproved, incomplete, inconsistent, or cannot be reproduced for the auditor-selected sample.

metadata.expected_evidence: Cryptographic dependency inventory, ownership, key and certificate lifecycle, escrow and backup, algorithm and expiry monitoring, recovery or re-encryption tests, access controls and logs, destruction rules, and technology-refresh plan. Acceptance requires tested continuity and no single undocumente
metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7, 12, 16, and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(c) and 11.10(d); NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 SC and CP controls as nonbinding guidance.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-14-020]: Demonstrate how personal data is minimized and deleted or anonymized when no longer lawfully required while regulated records, legal holds, audit trails, and evidentiary integrity remain protected.
Phase: Decommissioning, Data Retention & Migration | Domain: Data Privacy | Topic: Retention-limited deletion and minimization | Priority: High
Follow-Up Probe: Select one deletion request or expired personal-data class that intersects a GxP record and show the legal basis, field-level disposition, propagation to replicas and exports, and proof that the retained record remains complete and meaningful.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Data inventory and classification, lawful-basis and retention mapping, minimization and deletion rules, legal-hold checks, field-level design, anonymization validation where used, propagation to archives, replicas, and suppliers, execution logs, exceptions, and approvals. Acceptance requires lawful, consistent, and auditable disposition without loss of required GxP evidence.
Regulatory Alignment: GDPR Articles 5, 17, 25, 30, and 32 where applicable; EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7, 9, and 17; applicable predicate-rule retention requirements.
Red Flags: All data retained indefinitely as GxP; deletion breaks audit trail or attribution; replicas and supplier copies ignored; anonymization reversible or unvalidated; legal hold not checked; deletion evidence unavailable.

metadata.expected_evidence: Data inventory and classification, lawful-basis and retention mapping, minimization and deletion rules, legal-hold checks, field-level design, anonymization validation where used, propagation to archives, replicas, and suppliers, execution logs, exceptions, and approvals. Acceptance requires lawful,
metadata.reference: GDPR Articles 5, 17, 25, 30, and 32 where applicable; EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7, 9, and 17; applicable predicate-rule retention requirements.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-14-021]: Account for every backup, replica, snapshot, export, staging area, test copy, disaster-recovery environment, and removable medium and demonstrate its approved retention, access restriction, migration, expiry, or destruction.
Phase: Decommissioning, Data Retention & Migration | Domain: Backup & Data Disposition | Topic: Residual copies and backup retirement | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Select a copy outside the primary production account or data center and prove who can restore it, which keys and software it needs, when it expires, how legal holds apply, and how destruction is verified.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Copy topology and inventory, backup and snapshot catalogues, DR and test environments, exports and media register, retention and hold rules, access, key dependencies, expiration or destruction jobs, certificates, and reconciliation. Acceptance requires complete accounting and no restorable uncontrolled copy.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7.2, 12, 16, and 17; 21 CFR 211.68(b); GDPR Articles 5 and 32 where personal data apply; NIST SP 800-88 Rev. 2 as nonbinding sanitization guidance.
Red Flags: Copy inventory incomplete; snapshots in personal or supplier account; no expiry; restore access retained broadly; legal hold not propagated; test copies forgotten; destruction claimed without verification; keys persist after data destruction.

metadata.expected_evidence: Copy topology and inventory, backup and snapshot catalogues, DR and test environments, exports and media register, retention and hold rules, access, key dependencies, expiration or destruction jobs, certificates, and reconciliation. Acceptance requires complete accounting and no restorable uncontrol
metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7.2, 12, 16, and 17; 21 CFR 211.68(b); GDPR Articles 5 and 32 where personal data apply; NIST SP 800-88 Rev. 2 as nonbinding sanitization guidance.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-14-022]: Demonstrate the controlled sequence used to stop interfaces, jobs, APIs, file transfers, notifications, monitoring, user accounts, service accounts, certificates, tokens, remote support, and network routes without losing late data or leaving unauthorized pathways.
Phase: Decommissioning, Data Retention & Migration | Domain: Interface & Identity Shutdown | Topic: Orderly termination of technical pathways | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Show live telemetry after the claimed shutdown and explain any authentication attempt, network connection, scheduled execution, queue item, file arrival, or data write, including how it was contained and reconciled.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Shutdown plan and dependency order, cut-off and queue reconciliation, interface partner confirmation, job and account inventories, revocation and route changes, monitoring period, live telemetry, exceptions, and approvals. Acceptance requires zero unresolved traffic, active identity, or late data after final cut-off.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 5, 10, 12, 13, 16, and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(d), 11.10(g), and 11.300 where Part 11 applies.
Red Flags: Interfaces stopped before queues reconcile; service accounts active; certificates or tokens valid; late files discarded; network route remains; monitoring removed before observation period; partner not notified; live writes after shutdown.

metadata.expected_evidence: Shutdown plan and dependency order, cut-off and queue reconciliation, interface partner confirmation, job and account inventories, revocation and route changes, monitoring period, live telemetry, exceptions, and approvals. Acceptance requires zero unresolved traffic, active identity, or late data af
metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 5, 10, 12, 13, 16, and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(d), 11.10(g), and 11.300 where Part 11 applies.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-14-023]: Trace the supplier exit from contract obligations through complete data and metadata return, format usability, transition support, subprocessor coverage, access revocation, residual-copy destruction, evidence availability, and final service termination.
Phase: Decommissioning, Data Retention & Migration | Domain: Supplier Exit Management | Topic: Data return, continuity, and destruction | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Ask the supplier to account for primary, backup, replicated, support, telemetry, log, analytics, and subprocessor copies and compare the response with the shared-responsibility model and your own data-flow evidence.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Contract and Quality agreement exit clauses, data and copy inventory, export specification and reconciliation, transition and retrieval test, subprocessor attestations, access revocation, deletion or destruction certificate with scope and method, evidence and audit rights, and internal acceptance. document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-01-018]: Explain how proposed recovery objectives were derived from product, patient, data and operational impact, and show that exact and complete backup plus restoration verification are included in cost and responsibilities.
Phase: 01 Concept Business Case | Domain: Resilience | Topic: Backup, restoration and disaster recovery | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: For a corruption event discovered after several backup cycles, show which recovery point preserves both records and audit history and how post-restore reconciliation would detect lost transactions.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Business impact analysis; justified RTO/RPO; backup scope/frequency/immutability; restoration test plan; reconciliation and decision criteria; dependency map; supplier/internal responsibilities; periodic testing budget.
Regulatory Alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 211.68(b) and 11.10(c); Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§7 and 16; Guidance: MHRA §6.17, PIC/S §9.9 and WHO §§11.15-11.18.
Red Flags: RPO/RTO copied from supplier tier; restore never planned; audit trails/configuration omitted; backup cannot survive tenant/account compromise; no reconciliation after recovery.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-01-019]: Walk through the proposed business-continuity process during prolonged system or interface loss, including controlled manual records, approvals, inventory/status control and reconciliation after service restoration.
Phase: 01 Concept Business Case | Domain: Business Continuity | Topic: Operational continuity and manual fallback | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Simulate an outage spanning a batch, laboratory result and quality approval; identify where duplicate identifiers, back-dating or conflicting status could arise and how each is prevented.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Critical-process BIA; continuity workflow; controlled forms/logs; authority and communication rules; offline numbering/time controls; reconciliation and QA review; periodic exercise plan; maximum tolerable outage.
Regulatory Alignment: Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §16 and Chapter 4 §§4.7-4.9; Guidance: MHRA §§5.1, 6.20 and WHO §§4, 11.15-11.19.
Red Flags: Fallback stated as use paper without controlled forms; no reconciliation owner; outage records can be entered later without event time; continuity capacity untested.

Follow-Up Probe: Take a mandatory SaaS release scenario and explain how the company can obtain notice, assess GxP impact, test, reject or mitigate it before production exposure.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Lifecycle support model; change categories and gates; supplier-release process; configuration baseline; regression approach; emergency-change control; periodic evaluation scope/cadence; backlog and ownership. Red Flags: Go-live funding excludes operations; supplier releases bypass QA; no production baseline; periodic review is document expiry only; emergency changes remain unretrospectively approved.

Follow-Up Probe: Walk one hypothetical clock drift or audit-trail outage from monitoring alert to affected-record identification, batch/product impact, root cause, CAPA effectiveness and regulator/customer notification decision.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Integrated incident/deviation workflow; severity and GxP impact criteria; data population analysis; investigation/CAPA requirements; supplier notification SLAs; security/quality handoff; management and regulator escalation thresholds. Red Flags: Only service tickets planned; no affected-record search; supplier notification after root cause only; DI/security events excluded from QA; CAPA effectiveness not funded.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-01-022]: Demonstrate that the business case identifies the competencies and capacity needed for process ownership, configuration, validation, data review, administration, supplier oversight and support throughout the lifecycle.
Phase: 01 Concept Business Case | Domain: Training & Competence | Topic: Resource, competence and organizational change | Priority: High
Follow-Up Probe: Reconcile the named future-state roles with current headcount and training records, then show how coverage is maintained during turnover, absence and vendor transition.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Role/competency matrix; workload and segregation analysis; training curriculum and qualification criteria; succession/coverage plan; super-user limits; contractor oversight; recurring training and effectiveness measures; approved funding.
Regulatory Alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(i), 211.25 and 211.22; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §2; Guidance: FDA DI Q16, WHO §8 and ICH Q10 §2.
Red Flags: Key roles part-time with no workload analysis; training ends at go-live; supplier staff assumed qualified without evidence; incompatible duties assigned to one person; no backup personnel.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-01-023]: Present the major compliance assumptions and trade-offs in the approved business case and show how changes to cost, schedule or scope trigger independent quality reassessment and go/no-go decisions.
Phase: 01 Concept Business Case | Domain: Portfolio Governance | Topic: Cost, schedule and compliance trade-offs | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Select the largest cost reduction and shortest schedule assumption and trace their effect on supplier qualification, requirements, migration, testing, training, continuity and operational controls.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Decision log; assumptions register; quality gates; contingency and remediation reserves; independent QA approvals; escalation thresholds; benefits/schedule baseline; documented residual-risk acceptance by accountable management.
Regulatory Alignment: Binding quality-unit authority: 21 CFR 211.22; Guidance: ICH Q9(R1) §§3-5 and ICH Q10 §§2, 4; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §1.
Red Flags: QA lacks veto; launch date fixed before evidence; risk acceptance owned only by project; compliance contingency absent; critical deliverables removed without traceable decision.

Phase: 01 Concept Business Case | Domain: Data Integrity Culture | Topic: Benefits, KPIs and behavioral incentives | Priority: High
Follow-Up Probe: Take the most financially important KPI and demonstrate how a user could game it through data timing, status changes or exclusions, then show the preventive and detective controls funded.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Benefits/KPI catalogue; behavioral risk assessment; balanced quality metrics; definitions and data lineage; anti-gaming controls; escalation and speak-up channels; management review plan; culture/training actions. Acceptance: evidence is current, approved where required, complete for the selected population, and consistent with the live configuration and independent records.

Red Flags: Benefits depend on fewer deviations or faster closure without quality balance; excluded data improves KPI; audit data used punitively without culture controls; speak-up path absent.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-01-025]: Show how the concept funds an exit strategy that preserves readable GxP records, metadata, audit trails, signatures, configurations and retrieval capability after contract termination or technology obsolescence.
Phase: 01 Concept Business Case | Domain: Retirement & Exit | Topic: Decommissioning, portability and supplier exit | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Assume immediate supplier insolvency or account suspension and demonstrate how the company would obtain a complete, usable and verified record set plus the software, keys or viewer needed to inspect it.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Exit and decommission concept; data/export specifications; contractual assistance; escrow/viewer/key strategy where justified; verification and reconciliation; retention ownership; destruction authorization; budget and trigger points.
Regulatory Alignment: Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §17 and Chapter 4 §§4.10-4.12; Guidance: MHRA §§6.17, 6.20, PIC/S §§9.9-10 and WHO §§7, 11.15-11.19; ICH Q10 §3.1.4.
Red Flags: Exit cost omitted; proprietary export without metadata; supplier owns encryption keys; destruction may occur before QA approval; no supported long-term viewer or reconciliation criterion.

metadata.expected_evidence: Exit and decommission concept; data/export specifications; contractual assistance; escrow/viewer/key strategy where justified; verification and reconciliation; retention ownership; destruction authorization; budget and trigger points.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-02-001]: Explain how business, quality, technical and data owners converted the approved intended use into the URS, and show how conflicts, assumptions, exclusions and unresolved requirements are governed before design begins.
Phase: 02 URS | Domain: Governance | Topic: URS ownership, authorship and approval | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Select five requirements written or modified by the supplier and demonstrate the regulated-company SME who verified each business need, risk and acceptance criterion independently.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Controlled URS; author/reviewer competence; comments and resolution log; requirements governance/RACI; glossary; assumptions, constraints and exclusions; QA approval. Requirements are uniquely identified, versioned, unambiguous and owned. Acceptance: evidence is current, approved where required, complete for the selected population, and consistent with the live configuration and independent records.
Regulatory Alignment: Binding quality oversight: 21 CFR 211.22; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§2, 4.4 and Annex 15 §§2-3; Guidance: ICH Q10 §2.
Red Flags: Supplier copied its product specification into the URS; requirements lack owners or unique IDs; exclusions are implicit; approval predates workshops; QA comments were closed without evidence. Finding trigger: evidence is missing, unapproved, incomplete, inconsistent, or cannot be reproduced for the auditor-selected sample.

metadata.reference: Binding quality oversight: 21 CFR 211.22; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§2, 4.4 and Annex 15 §§2-3; Guidance: ICH Q10 §2.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-02-002]: Trace each intended use and predicate-record obligation into specific URS requirements for creation, review, approval, retention, retrieval and inspection, including functions outside the primary application boundary.
Phase: 02 URS | Domain: Regulatory Compliance | Topic: Intended use, predicate records and scope traceability | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Choose one downstream report used for release or quality disposition and demonstrate the requirement chain back to its source data, metadata, reviewer and governing record obligation.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Intended-use statement; GxP/Part 11 assessment; predicate-rule matrix; record/signature inventory; bidirectional concept-to-URS traceability; system-boundary diagram. Every regulated use and record has testable requirements or approved rationale.
Regulatory Alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.1-11.2, 11.10 and 211 Subpart J; Binding EU framework: Directive (EU) 2017/1572 Art. 9; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 Principle and §4.4.
Red Flags: Part 11 assessment not linked to requirements; reports/exports omitted from boundary; predicate records unnamed; requirements cover storage but not review, retrieval or inspection.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-02-003]: Show how critical process steps, data elements, metadata, calculations, reports and configurations are identified in the URS and linked to preliminary risk decisions without using priority labels as a substitute for compliance.
Phase: 02 URS | Domain: Quality Risk Management | Topic: Critical function and data classification | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Take a requirement marked low priority that handles a critical identifier or status and reconcile the rating with its downstream use and failure consequence.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Critical data/process inventory; requirement attributes for GxP impact and criticality; risk references; rationale and owners; rules separating business priority from quality risk; approved traceability.
Regulatory Alignment: Guidance: ICH Q9(R1) §§3-5; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§1 and 4.4; Guidance: MHRA §§4-5, PIC/S §5 and WHO §5.
Red Flags: MoSCoW priority used as risk; metadata/configuration not classified; low ratings lack causal rationale; criticality differs between URS and data inventory; mandatory controls marked optional.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-02-004]: Demonstrate how each URS statement expresses an observable outcome, boundary condition and acceptance criterion that can establish fitness for intended use rather than merely repeating policy words such as secure, compliant or user-friendly.
Phase: 02 URS | Domain: Validation Strategy | Topic: Testable requirements and acceptance criteria | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Select three high-risk requirements and show the positive, negative, boundary and failure-recovery evidence that could objectively prove each one before design is known.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Requirement quality checklist; measurable acceptance criteria; risk/test attributes; traceability conventions; verification method and responsible reviewer; approved ambiguity resolutions. Drug-GMP assurance is grounded in predicate rules/Annex 11, not a device-only CSA waiver.
Regulatory Alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(a) and 211.68; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§4.1, 4.4, 4.7 and Annex 15 §2; FDA guidance (nonbinding, device QMS scope only): CSA §V.A.
Red Flags: Subjective adjectives without measures; multiple controls bundled into one requirement; negative/error cases absent; acceptance delegated solely to supplier; CSA cited outside device scope to reduce evidence.

metadata.expected_evidence: Requirement quality checklist; measurable acceptance criteria; risk/test attributes; traceability conventions; verification method and responsible reviewer; approved ambiguity resolutions. Drug-GMP assurance is grounded in predicate rules/Annex 11, not a device-only CSA waiver.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-02-005]: Describe the URS requirements that preserve the full record context—originator, event time, system time, units, status, method, version, reason and relationships—from first capture through every transformation.
Phase: 02 URS | Domain: Data Integrity | Topic: Metadata, contemporaneity and ALCOA+ requirements | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Choose one displayed value and show every metadata element needed to reconstruct who did what, when and under which configuration; identify where the URS requires each element to be retained and reviewable.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Data/metadata dictionary; ALCOA+ requirement mapping; time-zone and clock rules; contemporaneous capture; provenance and lineage; completeness rules; review and retention requirements; controlled rationale for any excluded metadata.
Regulatory Alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(e) and 211.188/194; Official EU GMP guideline: Chapter 4 Principle and §§4.7-4.9; Guidance: FDA DI Q1, MHRA §§6.1-6.7 and WHO §4.
Red Flags: Only visible fields specified; event and entry times conflated; time zone absent; metadata may be overwritten; lineage ends at report; ALCOA+ appears only in a generic preamble.

metadata.expected_evidence: Data/metadata dictionary; ALCOA+ requirement mapping; time-zone and clock rules; contemporaneous capture; provenance and lineage; completeness rules; review and retention requirements; controlled rationale for any excluded metadata.

content:

Phase: 02 URS | Domain: Audit Trails | Topic: Audit-trail content, generation and protection | Priority: Critical

Red Flags: Requirement says audit trail available without event definition; prior values/reasons absent; privileged users can disable/delete logs; configuration/security events excluded; time source unspecified.

content:

Phase: 02 URS | Domain: Audit Trails | Topic: Risk-based audit-trail review and exception reporting | Priority: Critical

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-02-008]: Demonstrate how the URS specifies unique attribution, role-based least privilege, joiner/mover/leaver timing, periodic review and ownership for human, service, interface and robotic identities.
Phase: 02 URS | Domain: Access & Security | Topic: Unique identity and least-privilege requirements | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Map the full lifecycle of one external contractor and one nonhuman account, including creation approval, credential storage, allowed transactions, monitoring, review and revocation.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-02-009]: Explain how requirements separate record creation, approval, configuration, security administration, audit review and release, and how unavoidable conflicts and emergency access are independently authorized, logged and reviewed.
Phase: 02 URS | Domain: Access & Security | Topic: Privileged access, segregation and emergency control | Priority: Critical

Expected Evidence / Criteria: Segregation-of-duties rules; privileged access management; just-in-time/break-glass requirements; prohibition or control of direct database access; immutable admin logs; independent review; conflict approval/expiry; remote-support restrictions. content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-02-010]: Trace each regulated approval into URS requirements for signer identity, date/time, signature meaning, authentication, non-repudiation and permanent linkage to the exact record version and human-readable copy.

content:

content:

content:

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-03-005]: For each critical function, explain the credible failure modes and causal path from incorrect, missing, delayed or unauthorized system behavior to patient safety, product quality or supply impact.
Phase: 03 Risk GAMP | Domain: Patient/Product Risk | Topic: Failure modes and causal link to harm | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Take the top-rated and a low-rated failure mode and challenge both against worst credible use, existing detection time and the possibility of correlated failures across batches or sites.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Function-level hazard analysis; affected process/record/product; causal chain; severity rationale; failure detectability and timing; current/proposed controls; cross-batch/site exposure; residual risk and owner.
Regulatory Alignment: Guidance: ICH Q9(R1) §§3-5; Binding quality controls: 21 CFR 211.68 and 211.192; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §1.
Red Flags: Hazard is system failure with no consequence; severity lowered due to backup; correlated/batch-wide impact ignored; no product/process SME; risk inconsistent with release dependency.

content:

content:

Phase: 03 Risk GAMP | Domain: Interfaces | Topic: Transfer, transformation and reconciliation risk | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Interrupt a multi-record transfer after acknowledgement and reason through source/target states, retry, reconciliation, retained evidence and decision impact.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Interface risk register; field criticality; failure modes; source/target authority; controls for validation, acknowledgements, idempotency, reconciliation and alerts; error-queue ownership; residual risk and recovery.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-03-023]: Explain how defects, deviations, security events, audit findings, recalls, workarounds and prior changes from this product, supplier and predecessor system informed failure likelihood and control selection.
Phase: 03 Risk GAMP | Domain: Change & Incident Management | Topic: Historical evidence and change-induced risk | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Select a recurring legacy incident and demonstrate where its causal mechanism appears in the new risk assessment, URS, design control and planned effectiveness check.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Evidence review of deviations/incidents/CAPAs/complaints/audits; supplier defect history; lessons-learned traceability; change scenarios; affected controls; monitoring and effectiveness measures; justified exclusions.
Regulatory Alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 211.192 and 11.10(k); Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§10-13; Guidance: ICH Q9(R1) §4.6 and ICH Q10 §§3.2.2-3.2.4.
Red Flags: Risk workshop starts from blank template; known deviations absent; supplier defect history unavailable; lessons listed but not tied to controls; change risk only assessed after deployment.

metadata.expected_evidence: Evidence review of deviations/incidents/CAPAs/complaints/audits; supplier defect history; lessons-learned traceability; change scenarios; affected controls; monitoring and effectiveness measures; justified exclusions.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-03-024]: For every high or critical inherent risk, demonstrate that selected controls are specific, implemented by a named owner, testable, sustainable in operation and sufficient to justify the residual-risk conclusion.
Phase: 03 Risk GAMP | Domain: Risk Control | Topic: Control effectiveness and residual-risk ownership | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Remove the primary control for one high risk and show whether independent layers detect the failure before harm; explain any single-point dependence and monitoring threshold.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Control descriptions linked to requirements/design/SOP; owner and timing; preventive/detective nature; effectiveness evidence/acceptance criteria; dependencies and common cause; residual rationale; appropriate quality/management approval; open actions gated.
Regulatory Alignment: Guidance: ICH Q9(R1) §§4.4-4.6 and ICH Q10 §§2, 4; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §1; Guidance: WHO §5.
Red Flags: Future control credited as effective; owner is a department not person/role; residual score drops without evidence; single detective control acts after release; project manager accepts quality risk.

metadata.expected_evidence: Control descriptions linked to requirements/design/SOP; owner and timing; preventive/detective nature; effectiveness evidence/acceptance criteria; dependencies and common cause; residual rationale; appropriate quality/management approval; open actions gated.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-03-025]: Define the events and evidence that will trigger risk reassessment—requirements/design changes, supplier releases, incidents, drift, new threats, performance trends, periodic evaluation and retirement—and show how prior assumptions remain traceable.
Phase: 03 Risk GAMP | Domain: Risk Review | Topic: Dynamic reassessment and periodic risk review | Priority: High
Follow-Up Probe: Use a hypothetical supplier acquisition and security architecture change to demonstrate who detects the trigger, which risks reopen, how affected evidence is identified and who approves continued use.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Risk-review procedure; trigger catalogue and owners; links to change/incident/periodic review; version history; trend inputs; overdue-action escalation; reapproval and communication; retirement/legacy risks; scheduled cadence based on risk. Acceptance: evidence is current, approved where required, complete for the selected population, and consistent with the live configuration and independent records.
Regulatory Alignment: Guidance: ICH Q9(R1) §4.6 and ICH Q10 §§3.2.3-3.2.4, 4; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§10-11, 13; Guidance: PIC/S §5.6.
Red Flags: Review only at fixed document expiry; supplier/security/AI changes not triggers; prior rationale overwritten; risk actions can remain overdue through release; no owner monitors assumptions.

metadata.expected_evidence: Risk-review procedure; trigger catalogue and owners; links to change/incident/periodic review; version history; trend inputs; overdue-action escalation; reapproval and communication; retirement/legacy risks; scheduled cadence based on risk. document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-04-001]: Explain how supplier criticality was determined from intended use, control reliance, data access, service substitutability, complexity and failure impact, and show how that rating set the depth of due diligence and approval.
Phase: 04 Supplier Qualification | Domain: Supplier Governance | Topic: Supplier criticality and qualification depth | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Compare two suppliers with the same questionnaire score but different GxP reliance; demonstrate why their audit, evidence and ongoing-monitoring plans differ.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Approved supplier-risk method; intended-use/control reliance map; criticality rationale; due-diligence/audit plan; evidence gaps; remediation and approval authority; requalification triggers. Assessment depth is risk-based and independent of spend or brand.
Regulatory Alignment: Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§1, 3; Guidance: PIC/S §§10.1-10.3, WHO §7, ICH Q9(R1) §§3-5 and ICH Q10 §2.7.
Red Flags: Tier based on annual spend; SaaS automatically low risk; subprocessor not rated; questionnaire determines approval without verification; remediation deferred until after contract/go-live.

metadata.expected_evidence: Approved supplier-risk method; intended-use/control reliance map; criticality rationale; due-diligence/audit plan; evidence gaps; remediation and approval authority; requalification triggers. Assessment depth is risk-based and independent of spend or brand.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-04-002]: Walk through the supplier QMS from leadership oversight through document control, training, deviation/CAPA, change, internal audit and management review, and demonstrate its effectiveness with recent records rather than policy statements.
Phase: 04 Supplier Qualification | Domain: Quality Management System | Topic: Supplier governance and QMS effectiveness | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Select a repeated defect or audit finding and trace investigation, root cause, CAPA, effectiveness check and management escalation; reconcile any recurrence with the supplier's closure decision.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Current QMS scope/certificates; procedures and organization; management-review metrics; internal audit; deviations/CAPA and effectiveness; training; document/record control; customer-impact escalation; quality independence. Sample records show timely, sustained control.
Regulatory Alignment: Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§3.2-3.4, 4.5; Guidance: PIC/S §§9.3, 10, WHO §7 and ICH Q10 §§2, 2.7, 4.
Red Flags: Certificate scope excludes product/service; CAPAs close without effectiveness; repeat findings hidden in separate systems; quality reports to sales/project; customer-impact assessment undocumented. Finding trigger: evidence is missing, unapproved, incomplete, inconsistent, or cannot be reproduced for the auditor-selected sample.

metadata.expected_evidence: Current QMS scope/certificates; procedures and organization; management-review metrics; internal audit; deviations/CAPA and effectiveness; training; document/record control; customer-impact escalation; quality independence. Sample records show timely, sustained control.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-04-003]: Demonstrate how the supplier controls requirements, architecture, secure coding, code review, configuration, testing, release, maintenance and retirement for the exact product and version proposed.
Phase: 04 Supplier Qualification | Domain: Software Lifecycle | Topic: Supplier SDLC and product lifecycle controls | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Trace one high-impact requirement from backlog through code/configuration, review, test, defect disposition, build and released version; explain every missing link.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Lifecycle procedures; version control and branch/review rules; requirements/design/test traceability; build/release integrity; environment segregation; defect/change records; support/EOL policy; sample end-to-end trace for current version.
Regulatory Alignment: Binding customer validation duty: 21 CFR 11.10(a), 211.68; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§3, 4.5-4.7, 10; Guidance: PIC/S §§9.2-9.3.
Red Flags: Policies not applied to sampled release; no code review; production build not traceable to tested artifact; hotfix bypasses lifecycle; custom/configured components excluded; EOL surprise.

metadata.expected_evidence: Lifecycle procedures; version control and branch/review rules; requirements/design/test traceability; build/release integrity; environment segregation; defect/change records; support/EOL policy; sample end-to-end trace for current version.

content:

Phase: 04 Supplier Qualification | Domain: Supplier Maturity | Topic: Regulated experience, performance history and viability | Priority: High
Follow-Up Probe: Assume acquisition, key-person loss or product discontinuation within two years; demonstrate which evidence and contractual/technical controls preserve support and GxP records.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-04-005]: Walk through the deployed architecture and identify standard functions, tenant configuration, custom code, low-code components, reports, integrations and shared services, showing which lifecycle evidence and owner covers each.
Phase: 04 Supplier Qualification | Domain: Architecture | Topic: Product architecture, configuration and customization transparency | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Reconcile the supplier's standard-product claim with the actual object inventory and demonstrate how hidden extensions or customer-specific scripts are versioned, tested and supported.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Current architecture; component/version inventory; standard/configured/custom classification; extension repositories; supported configuration rules; dependency/bill-of-material evidence; ownership and support boundaries; customer-specific baseline.

Red Flags: Architecture is marketing-level; tenant customizations unlisted; production baseline cannot be exported; unsupported scripts used; component versions unknown; supplier/customer ownership overlaps.

content:

Phase: 04 Supplier Qualification | Domain: Validation Evidence | Topic: Supplier documentation and customer-use applicability | Priority: Critical

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-04-007]: Trace how test data, expected results, execution identity/time, environment, actual outcomes, deviations and defects are controlled so that passing status cannot be created by excluding failed or repeated runs.
Phase: 04 Supplier Qualification | Domain: Testing & Defects | Topic: Test integrity, deviations and defect transparency | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Choose a test with multiple executions and reconcile every run, failure, changed expected result, defect and final release decision from immutable source evidence.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Controlled test management; original execution evidence and audit history; environment/build identity; all runs retained; deviation/defect linkage; retest prerequisites; severity/customer-impact rationale; release acceptance and known-issue disclosure.
Regulatory Alignment: Binding customer duty: 21 CFR 11.10(a), 211.68; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§4.6-4.7; Guidance: FDA DI principles Q2-Q3 and WHO §§11.1-11.5.
Red Flags: Failed runs deleted; expected result changed after execution; environment/build absent; defects closed as user error without investigation; customer-impacting known issues withheld; screenshots are sole evidence.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-04-008]: Explain how the supplier's security governance, risk management, independent assessments and certifications apply to the exact service, regions and subprocessors, and how gaps are translated into GxP risk rather than accepted by badge.
Phase: 04 Supplier Qualification | Domain: Cybersecurity | Topic: Security governance and assurance reports | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Select one certification control exception and one penetration-test finding; trace remediation, residual exposure, customer notification and the GxP functions that depend on the control.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Security governance/RACI; current independent reports and scope; statement of applicability; penetration/vulnerability results; remediation evidence; incident metrics; customer control dependencies; risk acceptance and ongoing evidence schedule.
Regulatory Alignment: Binding GxP: 21 CFR 11.10(c)-(e), 11.30; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§3, 7, 12-13; Supplementary non-GxP: NIST SP 800-53 and ISO/IEC 27001.
Red Flags: Certificate scope excludes service/region; exceptions unavailable; pen-test summary is stale; security evidence treated as GxP validation; remediation dates conflict with risk acceptance.

metadata.expected_evidence: Security governance/RACI; current independent reports and scope; statement of applicability; penetration/vulnerability results; remediation evidence; incident metrics; customer control dependencies; risk acceptance and ongoing evidence schedule.

content:

Follow-Up Probe: Trace one terminated supplier engineer and one emergency production access event through HR source, approval, MFA, session record, actions, review and revocation across all regions.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Supplier IAM/PAM procedures; unique identity/MFA; role and tenant isolation; joiner/mover/leaver evidence; just-in-time/break-glass; session/action logs; independent review; customer notification; service-account ownership and secrets. Red Flags: Shared support IDs; customer cannot see privileged actions; leaver evidence sampled only locally; emergency access permanently enabled; subcontractors outside access review; direct database access unlogged.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-04-010]: Show how the product automatically captures and protects who, what, when and why for relevant record, configuration, master-data, access and administrator events, including prior/new values and customer control over enablement.
Phase: 04 Supplier Qualification | Domain: Audit Trails | Topic: Native audit-trail capability and tenant control | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: In a sandbox, alter, delete, reprocess and restore data, change a role and attempt to disable logging; reconcile every action to the resulting trail and immutable backend evidence.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Event catalogue; field-level demonstrations; reason rules; trusted timestamps; immutable/protected storage; enablement/defaults; privileged-event coverage; retention/export/search; trail configuration baseline; known limitations and remediation.
Regulatory Alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(e); Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §9; Guidance: MHRA §6.13, PIC/S §9.6 and WHO §§11.10-11.12.
Red Flags: Logs show only current value; no reason; supplier admin can disable/delete; audit trail off by default; tenant cannot export; configuration/access events missing; timestamps differ across services.

metadata.expected_evidence: Event catalogue; field-level demonstrations; reason rules; trusted timestamps; immutable/protected storage; enablement/defaults; privileged-event coverage; retention/export/search; trail configuration baseline; known limitations and remediation.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-04-011]: Walk through the shared-responsibility model and demonstrate how tenant isolation, configuration boundaries, monitoring, backup, encryption, changes and evidence delivery operate for the proposed service architecture.
Phase: 04 Supplier Qualification | Domain: Cloud Architecture | Topic: Tenancy, shared responsibility and control observability | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Assume a neighboring tenant exploit and a provider control failure; show how customer data exposure or corruption is prevented, detected, bounded, reported and evidenced.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Detailed architecture/data-flow; responsibility matrix to control level; tenant-isolation evidence; control-plane access; configuration boundaries; monitoring and evidence catalogue; regions/dependencies; customer controls and residual gaps. Acceptance: evidence is current, approved where required, complete for the selected population, and consistent with the live configuration and independent records.
Regulatory Alignment: Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §3; Guidance: MHRA §6.20, PIC/S §10 and WHO §7; Supplementary: NIST SP 800-53 SA-9 and access/audit control families.
Red Flags: RACI at provider/customer level only; tenant-isolation evidence absent; customer cannot observe control performance; shared control assigned to both or neither; hidden regional dependency.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-04-012]: Identify every subprocessor that can host, access, change, transmit, back up or support GxP data/services, and demonstrate risk-based qualification, contractual flow-down and ongoing change control.
Phase: 04 Supplier Qualification | Domain: Subcontractor Management | Topic: Subprocessor qualification and flow-down | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Select the least visible fourth-party service and trace its access, location, control evidence, incident/change obligations and removal contingency to the customer agreement.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Complete subprocessor register; service/data/access mapping; qualification evidence; flow-down of quality/security/retention/audit/incident/change duties; advance notice and objection rights; monitoring and exit alternatives.
Regulatory Alignment: Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §3; Guidance: MHRA §6.20, PIC/S §10, WHO §7 and ICH Q10 §2.7.
Red Flags: Supplier says no subcontractors but cloud services exist; list is incomplete or marketing-only; no advance notice/objection; flow-down excludes inspection access; fourth-party incidents need not reach customer.

content:

Red Flags: Location described only as global; logs/backups omitted; supplier can withhold data; customer lacks keys/export during suspension; deletion schedule conflicts with retention; support copies ungoverned.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-04-014]: Demonstrate how the supplier specifies, tests and controls interface schemas, transformations, authentication, acknowledgements, retries, idempotency, error handling, version compatibility and retained transmission evidence.
Phase: 04 Supplier Qualification | Domain: Interfaces & APIs | Topic: Integration reliability, versioning and evidence | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Recreate a breaking API change, partial payload and repeated retry; show customer notification, version coexistence, detection, reconciliation and records retained for investigation.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Versioned interface/API specifications; field mappings; security; compatibility/deprecation policy; test evidence; monitoring/error queues; control totals/reconciliation; change notice; log retention; support ownership.
Regulatory Alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(a)-(c), (h), 211.68; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§4.8, 5; Guidance: PIC/S §9.4 and WHO §9.
Red Flags: API can change without notice; mapping omits metadata; no idempotency/reconciliation; supplier deletes error logs quickly; authentication relies on shared credential; deprecation shorter than change cycle.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-04-015]: Show the exact backup scope, schedules, retention, isolation, encryption, monitoring and restoration process for tenant data, metadata, audit trails, configuration, files and keys.
Phase: 04 Supplier Qualification | Domain: Backup & Recovery | Topic: Backup completeness and restore verification | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Select a completed restoration test and reconcile source and restored counts, hashes, relationships, audit history, application usability and exceptions rather than relying on job success status.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Backup architecture/inventory; RPO coverage; immutable/separate protection where justified; monitored jobs; tenant-level and regional restore; periodic test plan/results; data integrity reconciliation; failure CAPA; customer evidence and responsibilities.
Regulatory Alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 211.68(b), 11.10(c); Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §7; Guidance: MHRA §6.17, PIC/S §9.9 and WHO §§11.15-11.18.
Red Flags: Audit trails/configuration/keys excluded; restore tests are infrastructure-only; tenant restoration unavailable; backup shares admin domain; test exceptions not investigated; customer receives no evidence.

metadata.expected_evidence: Backup architecture/inventory; RPO coverage; immutable/separate protection where justified; monitored jobs; tenant-level and regional restore; periodic test plan/results; data integrity reconciliation; failure CAPA; customer evidence and responsibilities.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-04-016]: Demonstrate how the supplier derived and tested availability, capacity, RTO and RPO across application and external dependencies, and how customers are informed and supported during regional or prolonged disruption.
Phase: 04 Supplier Qualification | Domain: Business Continuity | Topic: Resilience, capacity and disaster recovery | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Walk through the most recent exercise or real outage from detection to failover, data reconciliation, customer communication, return to normal and corrective actions, reconciling actual times with SLA claims.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-04-017]: Demonstrate that the service can retain and retrieve complete readable records—including metadata, audit trails, attachments, signatures and relationships—for customer-defined periods and provide accurate human-readable and electronic copies promptly.
Phase: 04 Supplier Qualification | Domain: Records & Inspection | Topic: Retention, archive, export and inspector access | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Retrieve an old, corrected and signed record from a nonproduction archive into both native and inspection formats; reconcile content, history, timing and searchability to the active record model.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Configurable retention; archive design/viewer; metadata/audit/signature preservation; legal hold and purge control; retrieval SLAs; export schemas and completeness verification; inspector/regulator access; format migration and readability tests.

Red Flags: Vendor retention is shorter; exports omit audit/signature history; archive requires unsupported client; inspector retrieval depends on paid professional service; purge can bypass customer QA; old data unreadable. content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-04-022]: Demonstrate how remote support is requested, authorized, time-limited, supervised, recorded and reviewed, including direct database/file access, data extracts, diagnostic copies and actions performed outside application controls.
Phase: 04 Supplier Qualification | Domain: Support Operations | Topic: Remote support, direct access and service records | Priority: Critical

Expected Evidence / Criteria: Approved functional/design specifications; unique IDs and revision control; URS/risk-to-design bidirectional traceability; decision/comment log; interface/procedure allocations; test method and acceptance links; independent QA/SME approval; no unexplained orphan or many-to-one mappings.

Red Flags: Traceability populated before design review; requirements mapped to headings not mechanisms; procedural controls have no SOP owner; supplier backlog conflicts with approved design; orphan risks or tests.

content:

content:

Expected Evidence / Criteria: Privileged-role matrix; PAM/just-in-time design; dual authorization where warranted; break-glass identity and expiry; session/command logging outside admin control; direct-data-change prohibition/controlled procedure; independent review; supplier access coverage. document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-05-008]: Explain how identity proofing, unique identifiers, MFA, credential issuance/reset, lockout, session timeout, reauthentication and nonhuman secrets are designed across normal, offline, recovery and support modes.
Phase: 05 Functional Design | Domain: Authentication | Topic: Identity provider, credential and session design | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Take over a dormant session, reset a signer's credential and rotate an interface secret; show how identity, prior signatures, service continuity, logs and investigation evidence remain reliable.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Authentication flows and trust boundaries; identity source and immutable identifier; MFA/risk controls; reset/recovery; session/token lifetimes; lockout; service-secret vault/rotation; IdP outage/failover; authentication logs and time synchronization. Acceptance: evidence is current, approved where required, complete for the selected population, and consistent with the live configuration and independent records.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-05-012]: For every critical formula and rule, identify authoritative inputs, source reference, version, units, precision, rounding, boundary/missing-data behavior, effective date and stored evidence needed to reproduce the result.
Phase: 05 Functional Design | Domain: Calculations | Topic: Formula, rule, precision and reproducibility design | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Calculate just below, at and above a decision boundary, then change an input or rule version and show how prior and recomputed outcomes remain distinguishable and reviewable.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Approved calculation/rule specifications; exact formula/decision table; input provenance; unit and precision conventions; null/error behavior; version/effective dating; independent oracle; stored result lineage; recalculation and downstream-impact rules.
Regulatory Alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(a), 211.68, 211.194; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§4, 6; Guidance: FDA DI Q3 and WHO §§9, 11.
Red Flags: Formula described in prose only; rounding in code but not spec; missing data treated silently; version absent from result; same implementation used as expected-value oracle; recalculation overwrites history.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-05-013]: Walk each critical field and metadata element through the interface design, including schema/version, source authority, transformation, precision, authentication, sequencing, acknowledgement, retry, idempotency, error queue and reconciliation.
Phase: 05 Functional Design | Domain: Interfaces | Topic: Data contract, transformation, retry and reconciliation design | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Model partial delivery followed by timeout, replay and source correction; derive source/target states, duplicate prevention, retained evidence, alerts and resolution ownership.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Versioned interface/data-contract specification; source-target mapping; transformations; message IDs/control totals; authentication/encryption; acknowledgement/retry/idempotency; time semantics; error quarantine; monitoring/reconciliation; retention and change compatibility.
Regulatory Alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(a)-(c), (h), 211.68; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§4.8, 5; Guidance: MHRA §§6.8-6.9, PIC/S §9.4 and WHO §9.
Red Flags: Mapping excludes units/metadata; retries not idempotent; error queue can be purged; no end-to-end control total; source/target authority differs by document; schema can change silently.

metadata.expected_evidence: Versioned interface/data-contract specification; source-target mapping; transformations; message IDs/control totals; authentication/encryption; acknowledgement/retry/idempotency; time semantics; error quarantine; monitoring/reconciliation; retention and change compatibility.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-05-014]: Demonstrate how critical configuration, specifications, limits, methods, templates and reference data are created, verified, approved, activated, versioned, linked to records, changed, rolled back and retired.
Phase: 05 Functional Design | Domain: Configuration & Master Data | Topic: Controlled parameter and reference-data lifecycle | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Backdate a limit and modify a workflow parameter; show which permissions, effective-date constraints, audit events, impact assessment and existing-record links prevent silent retrospective behavior change.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Critical-item catalogue; data/configuration model; role/segregation; dual verification by risk; workflow and effective dating; version linkage to transactions; audit event; import/migration reconciliation; change/rollback; environment promotion and baseline controls.
Regulatory Alignment: Binding: 21 CFR 11.10(e), (g), (k), 211.68; Official EU GMP guideline: Annex 11 §§4, 10, 12; Guidance: MHRA §§6.12-6.16.
Red Flags: Critical configuration not distinguished; creator self-approves; backdating unrestricted; records do not store applied version; direct import bypasses workflow; rollback erases intervening history.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-05-015]: Show how each report and export is derived from authoritative data and preserves required context, filters, units, versions, metadata, signatures and audit history so the output is accurate, complete and readily inspectable.
Phase: 05 Functional Design | Domain: Records & Inspection | Topic: Report, export and accurate-copy design | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Generate the same report with default, hidden and user-selected filters for a record containing corrections and excluded values; reconcile every difference to documented rules and visible report parameters.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Report/export catalogue; approved query and data lineage; filter/default visibility; template/version control; units/rounding; pagination/completeness totals; signature/audit metadata; native and human-readable formats; copy verification, performance and inspector access.

content:

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-05-019]: Walk through design behavior during application, interface, identity, network and supplier outages, including controlled offline records, unique identifiers, event times, authority, queued transactions and complete reconciliation after recovery.

Follow-Up Probe: Simulate two sites working offline while messages queue and a record is corrected in the source; show conflict resolution, chronology, duplicate prevention, approvals and QA-visible reconciliation evidence.

content:

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-05-021]: Demonstrate how specifications, code, configuration, master data, infrastructure and supplier releases are versioned, promoted through segregated environments, impact-assessed, tested, approved, deployed and rolled back while preserving the production baseline.

Follow-Up Probe: Trace an emergency configuration fix from detection to production and retrospective review, then prove which exact baseline was active for records created before, during and after the change.

content:
