content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-05-023]: Reconcile the technical design with the quality agreement and shared-responsibility matrix for tenant configuration, privileged access, audit evidence, change, backup, incidents, data location, subprocessors, inspection and exit.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-08-011]: Demonstrate through adverse testing that electronic signatures remain unique, authenticated, meaning-specific, time-stamped, permanently linked, and non-transferable when records are copied, changed, exported, restored, or viewed later.

Expected Evidence / Criteria: Evidence: signature requirements, role/identity setup, adverse tests, signed record, audit trail, copy/export, restore result, and credential logs. Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 14; 21 CFR 11.50, 11.70, 11.100, 11.200 and 11.300.

content:

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:

Follow-Up Probe: Inject a duplicate, missing sequence, invalid schema, transformed unit, delayed message, and target outage; show detection, quarantine, retry, reconciliation, and audit evidence.

content:

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-08-018]: Show how OQ challenges component failure and failover while proving transaction consistency, controlled user experience, alerting, recovery timing, and return to normal service without untraceable manual intervention.
Phase: 08 OQ | Domain: BCP | Topic: Failover and continuity controls | Priority: Critical

Expected Evidence / Criteria: Evidence: continuity architecture, failure scenarios, OQ raw logs, transaction reconciliation, alerts, recovery timing, failback evidence, and deviations. GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-10-020]: Demonstrate that all production endpoints, credentials, certificates, routes, queues, schedules, calendars, dependencies, alerts, and reconciliations were activated and verified without creating uncontrolled test or duplicate records.
Phase: 10 GoLive Handover | Domain: Interfaces & Integrations | Topic: Production interface, job, and scheduler verification | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Trace the first production transaction and first scheduled run end to end, including source authorization, middleware, target, control totals, alerts, retries, and business confirmation.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Evidence: production interface/job inventory, approved configuration, endpoint/credential/certificate checks, activation plan, first-run records/logs, reconciliation, alerts, and approvals. Acceptance: destinations and timing are correct; test paths are disabled; first transactions reconcile completely; failures are visible and owned.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.3, 5, 10 and 13; 21 CFR 11.10(a), 11.10(f), 11.10(h) and 11.30, where applicable.
Red Flags: Test endpoint/credential remains; first run not reconciled; schedule manually edited; duplicate startup run; certificate unverified; monitoring not active.

Acceptance: destinations and timing are correct; test paths are disabled; first transactions reconcile complet
metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.3, 5, 10 and 13; 21 CFR 11.10(a), 11.10(f), 11.10(h) and 11.30, where applicable.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-10-021]: Show how retention, legal/quality hold, archive, deletion, readability, integrity, and retrieval controls were configured and operational for each regulated record type before production records accumulated.
Phase: 10 GoLive Handover | Domain: Data Integrity | Topic: Retention, archive, and retrieval readiness | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: For one record with the longest retention and one with attachments/audit history, trace configured lifecycle rules, storage, holds, access, archive format, retrieval test, and prevention of premature deletion.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Evidence: record inventory and retention requirements, configuration exports, archive design, holds, deletion controls, access, readability/integrity test, retrieval procedure, and owner approval. Acceptance: rules match approved requirements; related metadata/audit/signatures remain linked; deletion is authorized and traceable; retrieval is tested.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7, 9 and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(b)-11.10(c) and applicable predicate-rule retention requirements such as 21 CFR 211.180.
Red Flags: Vendor default retention; audit/attachments excluded; archive unreadable without source system; deletion job active before approval; hold not tested; owner unknown.

Acceptance: rules match approved requirements; related metadata/audit/signatures remain linked; deletio
metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7, 9 and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(b)-11.10(c) and applicable predicate-rule retention requirements such as 21 CFR 211.180.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:

Phase: 10 GoLive Handover | Domain: Documentation & SOP | Topic: System inventory and description handover | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Select a production component or data flow by direct discovery and trace it to the inventory, system description, CMDB/cloud record, owner, support, backup, monitoring, and validation evidence.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Evidence: approved inventory/system description, as-built diagrams, data/interface inventory, component prerequisites, security and recovery controls, owners, validation status, CMDB/cloud reconciliation, and approval. Acceptance: records match production, are current and sufficiently detailed, and link all critical controls/owners.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 4.3 and Sections 2, 3 and 11.
Red Flags: Inventory lists application only; diagram not as-built; data flows/interfaces omitted; owner/support mismatch; validation status stale; cloud/service component missing.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-10-023]: Show how the validation summary report objectively reconciles planned and executed lifecycle evidence, deviations, changes, traceability, acceptance criteria, residual risk, and the precise released version before formal authorization for GxP use.
Phase: 10 GoLive Handover | Domain: CSV | Topic: Validation summary and formal release authorization | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Spot-check the report's most material conclusions against raw source records and explain any evidence created, revised, or approved after the stated release decision.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Evidence: approved validation summary, plan-to-actual reconciliation, traceability, protocol/report status, all deviations/defects/changes, residual risks, baseline/artifact identity, QA review, and formal release. Acceptance: claims reconcile to raw evidence; no unexplained gap exists; authorization precedes use; the released object is uniquely identified.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 15 Sections 2.9-2.10; EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.1-4.2; 21 CFR 11.10(a), where applicable.
Red Flags: Summary approved after use; totals mismatch; raw failures hidden; late changes omitted; release version unclear; QA review superficial; conditional approval not visible.

Acceptance: claims reconcile to raw evidence; no unexplained gap exists; authorizatio
metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 15 Sections 2.9-2.10; EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.1-4.2; 21 CFR 11.10(a), where applicable.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-10-024]: Where the system supports batch certification, product disposition, laboratory release, or another regulated release decision, demonstrate that only authorized roles can act and that the decision, identity, time, meaning, source evidence, and record status are complete at go-live.
Phase: 10 GoLive Handover | Domain: Governance & Risk Management | Topic: Regulated batch/release decision controls | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Attempt release with an unauthorized role, incomplete prerequisite, unresolved exception, altered supporting result, and disconnected signature service; show enforced blocks, evidence, and escalation.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Evidence: applicable release requirements, role/authority configuration, prerequisite/status rules, signature setup, production verification, audit trail, record copy, exception workflow, and responsible-owner acceptance. Acceptance: release is limited to authorized persons; prerequisites are enforced; decision and supporting evidence are attributable, complete, and retained.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 15 where batch certification/release applies, plus Sections 12 and 14; 21 CFR 11.10, 11.50 and 11.70 and applicable predicate rules such as 21 CFR 211.188/211.194.
Red Flags: Unauthorized role can release; prerequisites advisory only; signature meaning/record link absent; release ignores altered/incomplete source; exception bypass unlogged.

Acceptance: release is limited to authorized persons; prerequisites are enforc
metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 15 where batch certification/release applies, plus Sections 12 and 14; 21 CFR 11.10, 11.50 and 11.70 and applicable predicate rules such as 21 CFR 211.188/211.194.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-10-025]: Demonstrate how handover established the first periodic evaluation, access and audit-trail reviews, backup/restore checks, supplier reviews, vulnerability/patch governance, metrics, open-risk follow-up, and hypercare exit based on system risk.
Phase: 10 GoLive Handover | Domain: Periodic Review | Topic: Post-go-live control calendar and periodic evaluation | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: For each recurring control, show the first due date, population/data source, acceptance criteria, accountable owner, escalation, retained evidence, and mechanism that prevents the control from being missed after project closure.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Evidence: operational control calendar, risk-based frequencies, procedures, owners/backups, system-generated reminders, evidence repositories, KPI/KRI baselines, periodic-review plan, hypercare exit criteria, and governance approval. Acceptance: all recurring controls are scheduled and resourced; criteria and evidence are defined; open obligations transfer; overdue items escalate.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7.2, 9, 11-13 and 16; ICH Q10 Pharmaceutical Quality System guidance; ICH Q9(R1).
Red Flags: First review date absent; owner is project role; frequency arbitrary; no population/criteria; reminder manual and unowned; hypercare closes with open trends; risks not transferred.

metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7.2, 9, 11-13 and 16; ICH Q10 Pharmaceutical Quality System guidance; ICH Q9(R1).

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-11-001]: Reconstruct the most recent periodic evaluation from its source populations and show how the conclusion that the system remains fit for intended use, in a validated state, and compliant was reached.
Phase: 11 Ops Periodic Review | Domain: Periodic Review | Topic: Validated-state conclusion | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Identify the highest-risk unresolved item at the evaluation cut-off date, explain why it did not invalidate the conclusion, and show the approved interim control, accountable owner, due date, and subsequent status.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Approved periodic-evaluation procedure and report; frozen populations for changes, incidents, deviations, problems, access reviews, vulnerabilities, supplier changes, backup and recovery tests, performance, training, validation status, and open CAPA. Acceptance requires traceable source totals, documented scope and cut-off, risk-based conclusions, Quality approval, and controlled follow-up of every exception.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 1, 4.1, and 11; ICH Q9(R1) Sections 3 and 4; 21 CFR 11.10(a) where Part 11 applies.
Red Flags: Review based on curated summaries rather than complete populations; missing cut-off; overdue critical actions omitted; unapproved residual risk; conclusion copied from prior review; material conflicts between source systems and report.

Acceptance requires traceable source totals, docu
metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 1, 4.1, and 11; ICH Q9(R1) Sections 3 and 4; 21 CFR 11.10(a) where Part 11 applies.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-11-002]: Demonstrate that the approved system inventory entry and system description represent the live physical and logical arrangement, GxP functions, interfaces, data flows, prerequisites, hosting locations, and security boundaries as of today.
Phase: 11 Ops Periodic Review | Domain: Governance & Risk Management | Topic: Current inventory and system description | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: The auditor will select one live component or interface from monitoring and ask you to locate it in the inventory, architecture, configuration-management database, risk assessment, and support model; explain any discrepancy and its impact.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Current approved inventory, system description, architecture and data-flow diagrams, interface register, CMDB records, hosting and supplier inventory, and reconciliation record. Acceptance requires all live GxP-relevant components and dependencies to be uniquely identified, owned, versioned, and periodically reconciled.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.3 and 11; 21 CFR 11.10(a) and 11.10(k) where Part 11 applies.
Red Flags: Undocumented live components or interfaces; shared dependencies outside scope; obsolete diagrams; conflicting versions; missing owner; component absent from backup, monitoring, validation, or security scope.

metadata.expected_evidence: Current approved inventory, system description, architecture and data-flow diagrams, interface register, CMDB records, hosting and supplier inventory, and reconciliation record. Acceptance requires all live GxP-relevant components and dependencies to be uniquely identified, owned, versioned, and per
metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.3 and 11; 21 CFR 11.10(a) and 11.10(k) where Part 11 applies.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-11-003]: Using the complete current privileged-access population, demonstrate how each administrative entitlement is justified by job responsibility, independently approved, technically constrained, monitored, and periodically recertified.
Phase: 11 Ops Periodic Review | Domain: Access Management | Topic: Privileged-access recertification | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Select the most powerful role and show whether its holder can create or alter GxP data, change audit-trail settings, delete records, modify security, and approve their own work; explain the preventive or independently operating compensating controls.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Role catalogue, privilege matrix, named-user export, approval records, recertification results, segregation-of-duties analysis, privileged-session or activity logs, and exception records. Acceptance requires unique identities, least privilege, independence from regulated activity where feasible, timely exception removal, and documented monitoring of unavoidable conflicts.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 12.1 to 12.4; 21 CFR 11.10(d), 11.10(g), and 11.300 where Part 11 applies; 21 CFR 211.68(b) for drug CGMP systems.
Red Flags: Analysts or business users hold unrestricted administrator rights; shared admin credentials; unexplained local accounts; self-approval; incomplete technical population; overdue removal; audit logs unavailable or review performed by the same administrator.

metadata.expected_evidence: Role catalogue, privilege matrix, named-user export, approval records, recertification results, segregation-of-duties analysis, privileged-session or activity logs, and exception records. Acceptance requires unique identities, least privilege, independence from regulated activity where feasible, tim
metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 12.1 to 12.4; 21 CFR 11.10(d), 11.10(g), and 11.300 where Part 11 applies; 21 CFR 211.68(b) for drug CGMP systems.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-11-004]: Trace the joiner, mover, and leaver control from the authoritative HR event through identity-provider and application entitlements to prove that access is granted, changed, and removed within approved risk-based time limits.
Phase: 11 Ops Periodic Review | Domain: Access Management | Topic: Joiner-mover-leaver effectiveness | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: For an auditor-selected privileged leaver or mover, show every access path that survived the HR event, including local accounts, API tokens, remote-support accounts, cached credentials, group inheritance, and owned service accounts, and explain any activity after the effective time.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: HR source record, IAM workflow, application and infrastructure account exports, group membership, token and remote-access inventory, activity logs, service-account ownership transfer, SLA metrics, and exceptions. Acceptance requires end-to-end completeness, timely execution, no unexplained post-termination activity, and risk-assessed exceptions.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 12.1 and 12.3; 21 CFR 11.10(d) and 11.10(g) where Part 11 applies.
Red Flags: Sampling only completed tickets; termination timestamp later than observed activity; unmanaged local or vendor accounts; inherited entitlements omitted; service accounts still owned by leavers; no retrospective impact assessment for delayed removal.

metadata.expected_evidence: HR source record, IAM workflow, application and infrastructure account exports, group membership, token and remote-access inventory, activity logs, service-account ownership transfer, SLA metrics, and exceptions. Acceptance requires end-to-end completeness, timely execution, no unexplained post-term
metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 12.1 and 12.3; 21 CFR 11.10(d) and 11.10(g) where Part 11 applies.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-11-005]: Demonstrate how every non-human identity is inventoried, uniquely purposed, least-privileged, credential-managed, monitored, and assigned to a current accountable owner throughout operation.
Phase: 11 Ops Periodic Review | Domain: Access Management | Topic: Non-human and service accounts | Priority: High
Follow-Up Probe: Choose one high-privilege service account and show what prevents interactive use, credential sharing, unapproved secret extraction, and silent activity; then demonstrate the last credential rotation without disrupting or bypassing the validated process.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Service-account inventory, purpose and owner, entitlement mapping, vault records, rotation history, interactive-login restrictions, activity logs and alerts, dependency mapping, and exception approvals. Acceptance requires no orphaned identities, controlled secrets, attributable use, least privilege, and tested rotation or revocation.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 12.1 to 12.4; 21 CFR 11.10(d), 11.10(g), and 11.300 where Part 11 applies; NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 controls AC-2 and IA-5 as security guidance.
Red Flags: Unknown owner or purpose; shared credential in code or tickets; interactive login permitted without justification; no rotation; account activity outside expected jobs; inventory reconstructed manually for the audit.

metadata.expected_evidence: Service-account inventory, purpose and owner, entitlement mapping, vault records, rotation history, interactive-login restrictions, activity logs and alerts, dependency mapping, and exception approvals. Acceptance requires no orphaned identities, controlled secrets, attributable use, least privilege
metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 12.1 to 12.4; 21 CFR 11.10(d), 11.10(g), and 11.300 where Part 11 applies; NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 controls AC-2 and IA-5 as security guidance.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-11-006]: Using an auditor-selected GxP record, demonstrate how audit-trail review identifies, evaluates, and resolves every material creation, modification, deletion, reprocessing, status change, and security event relevant to the quality decision.
Phase: 11 Ops Periodic Review | Domain: Audit Trail | Topic: Risk-based audit-trail review | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Show the complete event population for the same record directly from the system, including events not displayed in the routine review report, and explain how reviewers detect missing periods, disabled logging, administrator activity, clock differences, or repeated attempts that did not change the final value.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Audit-trail configuration and risk assessment, review procedure and frequency, raw system-generated event export, reviewer record, linked source record, exception investigation, reviewer training, and periodic verification of audit-trail availability. Acceptance requires complete intelligible events, independent and timely review, documented reasons for GxP changes, and traceable resolution before the associated decision where required.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 9 and 12.4; 21 CFR 11.10(e); FDA Data Integrity and Compliance With Drug CGMP Q&A; PIC/S PI 041-1.
Red Flags: Audit trail disabled, configurable by conflicted users, incomplete, unintelligible, or unavailable; review limited to final values; missing reasons; unexplained gaps; late review after batch or quality decision; admin actions excluded.

metadata.expected_evidence: Audit-trail configuration and risk assessment, review procedure and frequency, raw system-generated event export, reviewer record, linked source record, exception investigation, reviewer training, and periodic verification of audit-trail availability. Acceptance requires complete intelligible events
metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 9 and 12.4; 21 CFR 11.10(e); FDA Data Integrity and Compliance With Drug CGMP Q&A; PIC/S PI 041-1.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-11-007]: Select a completed electronic signature and prove from the live record and underlying controls that the signer identity, date and time, signature meaning, credential use, and permanent linkage to the exact signed record version remain unambiguous and non-transferable.
Phase: 11 Ops Periodic Review | Domain: Electronic Signatures | Topic: Signature meaning and record linkage | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Demonstrate what happens when the signed record is subsequently corrected, migrated, exported, or archived, and show that the signature cannot be excised, copied to another record, or displayed against a changed version without an attributable event.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Signed record, signature manifestation, identity record, authentication configuration, signature and audit logs, record-version history, signature policy, and migration or archive test where relevant. Acceptance requires unique signer control, recorded name/date/time/meaning, permanent linkage, preservation after record lifecycle events, and no shared credentials.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 14; 21 CFR 11.50, 11.70, 11.100, 11.200, and 11.300 where Part 11 applies.
Red Flags: Signature not tied to a record version; missing meaning or timestamp; shared credentials; signature can be copied or detached; correction changes signed content without new signature; archive or export loses linkage.

metadata.expected_evidence: Signed record, signature manifestation, identity record, authentication configuration, signature and audit logs, record-version history, signature policy, and migration or archive test where relevant. Acceptance requires unique signer control, recorded name/date/time/meaning, permanent linkage, pres
metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 14; 21 CFR 11.50, 11.70, 11.100, 11.200, and 11.300 where Part 11 applies.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-11-008]: Retrieve an auditor-selected record from the oldest active retention cohort and demonstrate that its content, context, critical metadata, audit trail, and associated signatures remain accurate, readable, intelligible, and available for review without relying on undocumented expert intervention.
Phase: 11 Ops Periodic Review | Domain: Data Integrity | Topic: Retention-period accessibility and readability | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Repeat the retrieval for a record created before the latest major application, database, operating-system, or viewer change and explain how continued readability and meaning were verified when technology changed.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Retention schedule, record inventory, storage and archive architecture, retrieval procedure, periodic readability and integrity checks, sample record with metadata and audit trail, and technology-change impact assessments. Acceptance requires timely retrieval, complete content and context, verified integrity, controlled access, and documented remediation of failed checks.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7.1 and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(b) and 11.10(c) where Part 11 applies; applicable predicate-rule retention requirements.
Red Flags: Old records cannot be retrieved promptly; proprietary viewer unavailable; metadata or audit trail omitted; integrity checks never performed; retention period guessed; technology changes not assessed; reliance on an unsupported production environment.

metadata.expected_evidence: Retention schedule, record inventory, storage and archive architecture, retrieval procedure, periodic readability and integrity checks, sample record with metadata and audit trail, and technology-change impact assessments. Acceptance requires timely retrieval, complete content and context, verified
metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7.1 and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(b) and 11.10(c) where Part 11 applies; applicable predicate-rule retention requirements.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-11-009]: Reconcile the approved inventory of GxP data, metadata, audit trails, configurations, encryption material, and supporting components to the live backup job definitions and demonstrate that the backup scope remains complete after system changes.
Phase: 11 Ops Periodic Review | Domain: Backup & Disaster Recovery | Topic: Backup population completeness | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Select one newly added or changed component and one apparently successful backup; prove that the required content was actually captured and usable rather than merely that the job ended with a success status.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Data and component inventory, backup architecture and job definitions, retention and immutability settings, job and exception logs, scope reconciliation, change records, and content verification. Acceptance requires complete risk-based scope, monitored failures, protected copies, periodic reconciliation after change, and no unapproved exclusions.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 7.2; 21 CFR 211.68(b); 21 CFR 11.10(c) where Part 11 applies; NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 control CP-9 as security guidance.
Red Flags: Scope cannot be reconciled; successful status accepted without content verification; audit trails, attachments, or keys excluded; backup changes outside change control; failed jobs aged or suppressed; no protected off-system copy where risk requires it.

metadata.expected_evidence: Data and component inventory, backup architecture and job definitions, retention and immutability settings, job and exception logs, scope reconciliation, change records, and content verification. Acceptance requires complete risk-based scope, monitored failures, protected copies, periodic reconcilia
metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Section 7.2; 21 CFR 211.68(b); 21 CFR 11.10(c) where Part 11 applies; NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 control CP-9 as security guidance.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-11-010]: Reperform the evidence chain for the last recovery exercise and show that the recovered service met approved recovery time and recovery point objectives while preserving record completeness, data meaning, audit trails, interfaces, security, and business-process usability.
Phase: 11 Ops Periodic Review | Domain: Business Continuity | Topic: Restore and recovery effectiveness | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Show the last failed or partially successful restore step, how the failure was detected, what data interval or functionality was at risk, and whether the retest proved the corrective action rather than repeating only the successful path.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Approved recovery plan, business impact analysis, RTO and RPO, exercise protocol and raw timestamps, restored-data reconciliation, security and interface checks, business and Quality acceptance, deviations, CAPA, and retest. Acceptance requires objectives achieved or deviations formally assessed with effective remediation and no unexplained data loss.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7.2 and 16; 21 CFR 211.68(b); NIST SP 800-34 Rev. 1 and NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 CP controls as nonbinding guidance.
Red Flags: Restore never tested; test excludes audit trails, interfaces, keys, or business verification; RTO or RPO missed without risk acceptance; failed step omitted; recovered data not reconciled; exercise performed only on unlike infrastructure.

metadata.expected_evidence: Approved recovery plan, business impact analysis, RTO and RPO, exercise protocol and raw timestamps, restored-data reconciliation, security and interface checks, business and Quality acceptance, deviations, CAPA, and retest. Acceptance requires objectives achieved or deviations formally assessed wit
metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7.2 and 16; 21 CFR 211.68(b); NIST SP 800-34 Rev. 1 and NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 CP controls as nonbinding guidance.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-11-011]: Trace a complete GxP data transfer from authoritative source through middleware to target and downstream report, demonstrating how completeness, accuracy, sequence, attribution, timestamps, and processing status are reconciled in routine operation.
Phase: 11 Ops Periodic Review | Domain: Interfaces & Integrations | Topic: Operational reconciliation of data transfers | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Use the last failed, duplicate, delayed, partial, or out-of-order transfer and show how the system prevented silent loss or double processing, preserved the original event, controlled reprocessing, and assessed downstream quality impact.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Interface inventory and data mapping, control totals or acknowledgements, queue and transaction logs, error and retry configuration, reconciliation reports, incident or deviation, reprocessing record, and downstream verification. Acceptance requires end-to-end traceability, controlled error handling, no silent loss or duplication, and documented impact assessment.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 5, 7, 8, 9, and 13; 21 CFR 11.10(a), 11.10(e), 11.10(f), and 11.10(h) where Part 11 applies.
Red Flags: No end-to-end identifier or reconciliation; monitoring only transport availability; discarded error messages; uncontrolled replay; duplicate processing; manual correction outside audit trail; source and target totals disagree without investigation.

metadata.expected_evidence: Interface inventory and data mapping, control totals or acknowledgements, queue and transaction logs, error and retry configuration, reconciliation reports, incident or deviation, reprocessing record, and downstream verification. Acceptance requires end-to-end traceability, controlled error handling
metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 5, 7, 8, 9, and 13; 21 CFR 11.10(a), 11.10(e), 11.10(f), and 11.10(h) where Part 11 applies.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-11-012]: Starting from the full alert population, demonstrate how quality-relevant alarms are rationalized, prioritized, routed, acknowledged, investigated, and closed within defined limits, including periods when the primary responder is unavailable.
Phase: 11 Ops Periodic Review | Domain: Operations Monitoring | Topic: Alarm and alert response | Priority: High
Follow-Up Probe: Select one suppressed, auto-closed, repeated, or missed alert and reconstruct what occurred in the regulated process during the blind period; explain how the impact population was identified and why recurrence is controlled.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Alert catalogue and rationale, thresholds, routing and escalation rules, on-call coverage, raw alert history, acknowledgement and response records, suppression approvals, deviations or incidents, trend review, and effectiveness actions. Acceptance requires complete population visibility, risk-based response limits, controlled suppression, and impact assessment for missed alerts.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 1, 11, and 13; 21 CFR 211.68(a); ICH Q9(R1) Sections 3 and 4.
Red Flags: No complete alert population; alert floods or chronic recurrence; critical alert auto-closed; undocumented suppression; response SLA measured without quality impact; blind periods not assessed; no escalation outside business hours.

metadata.expected_evidence: Alert catalogue and rationale, thresholds, routing and escalation rules, on-call coverage, raw alert history, acknowledgement and response records, suppression approvals, deviations or incidents, trend review, and effectiveness actions. Acceptance requires complete population visibility, risk-based
metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 1, 11, and 13; 21 CFR 211.68(a); ICH Q9(R1) Sections 3 and 4.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-11-013]: Show how the periodic evaluation derives and challenges incident, deviation, problem, and service-request trends from complete source populations rather than relying on ticket labels or manually selected quality events.
Phase: 11 Ops Periodic Review | Domain: Incident & Deviation Management | Topic: Operational event trend inclusion | Priority: High
Follow-Up Probe: Reclassify a sample of low-severity or non-GxP-labelled tickets against the system's intended use and data flows; explain any event that should have triggered a deviation, validation impact assessment, or broader retrospective review.

Expected Evidence / Criteria: Approved baseline, automated or controlled configuration export, comparison report, parameter ownership, authorized change records, temporary-change expiry, drift alerts, investigation, and re-baselining approval. Red Flags: Assets missing from scan scope; risk accepted from CVSS alone; overdue critical vulnerabilities; compensating control asserted without telemetry; exception has no expiry; supplier constraint accepted indefinitely; patch not linked to validation impact.

Red Flags: Certification treated as complete evidence; expired bridge period; agreement omits GxP records or inspection access; supplier changes not notified; subprocessor unknown; exceptions not assessed; responsibility gap for backup, logs, incidents, or data return.

Follow-Up Probe: Identify the earliest evidence that existed before the official start time and show why monitoring, a user, or a supplier did not recognize it; quantify records and decisions created during the undetected interval.

Follow-Up Probe: Show each restart, rollback, log rotation, cache clear, file deletion, account disablement, or configuration change performed during response and prove that evidence was captured first or the loss was explicitly assessed.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Containment decision record, forensic or evidence-preservation procedure, native logs and snapshots, chain of custody where appropriate, responder actions, emergency changes, backup copies, and Quality oversight. Red Flags: System wiped or restarted before capture; logs overwritten; response actions use shared account; no original evidence; chain of custody unclear; emergency changes undocumented; evidence gap dismissed without impact assessment.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-13-012]: Demonstrate how the investigation distinguished root cause, contributing causes, detection-control failure, and organizational or process conditions using evidence that can reproduce and explain the observed event.
Phase: 13 Incident Problem Dev | Domain: Problem Management | Topic: Evidence-based root cause | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Present the strongest competing causal hypothesis, show the discriminating evidence used to reject it, and explain which facts remain uncertain and how that uncertainty changes corrective action or monitoring.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Problem statement, complete timeline, evidence catalogue, technical and process analysis, hypotheses, experiments or reproduction, causal chain, contributing factors, detection failure, uncertainty, cross-functional review, and approved conclusion. Acceptance requires evidence sufficient to explain occurrence and recurrence and actions addressing the causal mechanism.

content:

Expected Evidence / Criteria: Task analysis, procedure and training content, competence, workload and environment, access and UI controls, system checks, supervision, interviews, recurrence data, and redesigned controls. content:

content:

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-14-001]: Reconstruct the approved retirement decision and demonstrate how business, Quality, records, security, privacy, legal, supplier, continuity, and technical owners agreed the system boundary, timing, successor capability, retained obligations, and exit criteria.
Phase: 14 Decommission Retention | Domain: Decommissioning Governance | Topic: Retirement decision and scope | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Identify the strongest dependency or regulated use arguing against shutdown and show the objective evidence that it was replaced, archived, risk-controlled, or formally accepted before the final irreversible step.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Approved retirement business case, GxP and regulatory assessment, scope and dependency analysis, accountable owners, successor and archive decisions, risk assessment, legal and retention review, exit criteria, timeline, and Quality approval. Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 lifecycle principle and Sections 1, 4.3, 7, 16, and 17; ICH Q9(R1) Sections 3 and 4.
Red Flags: Retirement approved by project or IT alone; scope differs from live inventory; open deviations, legal holds, or regulated uses omitted; exit criteria vague; irreversible shutdown scheduled before evidence completion; Quality approval absent.

content:

Phase: 14 Decommission Retention | Domain: Configuration & Dependency Management | Topic: Complete dependency inventory | Priority: Critical

Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.3, 5, 10, 16, and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(a) and 11.10(k) where Part 11 applies.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-14-010]: Demonstrate how every migration exception is uniquely identified, preserved, investigated, risk-assessed, corrected under control, independently verified, reprocessed once, and included in final reconciliation.
Phase: 14 Decommission Retention | Domain: Migration Exceptions | Topic: Rejected and quarantined records | Priority: Critical

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-14-011]: Demonstrate that the migration or archive preserves every required audit event, prior value, new value, actor, timestamp, action, reason, record linkage, and review status in an intelligible and reviewable form.
Phase: 14 Decommission Retention | Domain: Audit Trail | Topic: Audit-trail preservation | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Compare a raw source audit-trail export with the target or archive for events created by administrators, failed actions, deletions, configuration changes, and periods where user-facing reports normally filter events.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Source audit schema and configuration, full event population, mapping, transformation rules, target or archive events, intelligible display and electronic copy, event and record linkage, review capability, reconciliation, and access control. Acceptance requires complete history and no loss of meaning or reviewability.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 9 and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(e); FDA Data Integrity Q&A; PIC/S PI 041-1.
Red Flags: Only audit-trail PDF retained; prior values or reasons omitted; admin or failed events filtered; record linkage broken; timestamps transformed without trace; audit events not searchable or reviewable; source destroyed before reconciliation.

content:

Phase: 14 Decommission Retention | Domain: Metadata & Hybrid Records | Topic: Time, attachments, and contextual integrity | Priority: High

Acceptance requires preserved association, meaning, chronology, and integrity.

Follow-Up Probe: Select a record created near the cutover boundary and show how duplicate creation, update in the wrong system, clock difference, and delayed interface delivery were detected and reconciled.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Cutover plan, freeze and authority matrix, synchronized timeline, user and interface controls, queue and backlog inventory, communication, boundary reconciliation, duplicate checks, deviations, and acceptance. Acceptance requires one unambiguous authoritative record for every interval and resolved transition exceptions.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.8, 5, 7, 9, 10, and 16; 21 CFR 11.10(a), 11.10(e), and 11.10(f).
Red Flags: Authority rule unclear; both systems writable; boundary times differ; late queue omitted; user access not aligned to freeze; duplicate records; manual backlog unreconciled; source changed after final extract.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-14-015]: Trace archive or migration risks and requirements to test scenarios, raw evidence, deviations, reconciliation, acceptance, and release, including boundary, negative, failure, recovery, and long-term retrieval cases.
Phase: 14 Decommission Retention | Domain: Validation / Assurance | Topic: Archive and migration verification | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Show the highest-risk requirement with reduced or no scripted testing and demonstrate why other objective evidence provides sufficient assurance; then present the last failed test and its full resolution chain.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Validation or assurance plan, risk and requirement trace, test strategy, controlled tools and environments, positive and negative tests, raw execution evidence, deviations and defects, reconciliation, retrieval and recovery tests, summary, and Quality approval. Acceptance requires assurance commensurate with risk and no unexplained failed requirement.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 4.1, 4.2, 4.7, 4.8, and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(a) where Part 11 applies; ICH Q9(R1) Section 3.
Red Flags: Testing focused on counts only; long-term retrieval omitted; failed test overwritten; automated tool unassessed; deviations open at release; traceability mechanical; excluded requirements unsupported; source destroyed before approval. Finding trigger: evidence is missing, unapproved, incomplete, inconsistent, or cannot be reproduced for the auditor-selected sample.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-14-016]: Retrieve an auditor-selected archived record without production-system access and demonstrate timely search, access, readability, integrity, intelligibility, audit history, signature linkage, and accurate human-readable and electronic copies.
Phase: 14 Decommission Retention | Domain: Archiving Operations | Topic: Retrieval, readability, and inspection copies | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Repeat the retrieval for the oldest cohort and for a record created before a major format, viewer, operating-system, or archive-platform change; explain every manual or specialist step required.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Archive search and retrieval procedure, access authorization, native or preserved representation, metadata and audit history, signature linkage, copies, integrity verification, retrieval SLA, platform-change tests, and exception handling. Acceptance requires reproducible timely retrieval with complete meaning and no dependence on the retired production environment.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7.1, 8, 9, 14, and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(b) and 11.10(c).
Red Flags: Retrieval requires retired application; oldest records unreadable; metadata or audit trail absent; signatures unresolved; electronic copy proprietary or incomplete; manual reconstruction undocumented; SLA missed without action.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-14-017]: Demonstrate how periodic checks prove archive accessibility, readability, integrity, security, backup, recovery, capacity, and viewer compatibility and how results trigger controlled technology refresh before records become at risk.
Phase: 14 Decommission Retention | Domain: Archiving Operations | Topic: Ongoing archive integrity and technology refresh | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Show the last failed integrity, retrieval, or compatibility check, identify every potentially affected object, and demonstrate correction, retrospective scope, retest, and trend action.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Periodic-check procedure and risk-based frequency, complete archive population, integrity and retrieval results, access and security reviews, backup and recovery tests, capacity and lifecycle monitoring, exceptions, remediation, refresh plan, and Quality review. Acceptance requires complete monitored coverage and effective response to failures.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7.1, 7.2, 11, 16, and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(c); NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 CP and SI controls as nonbinding guidance.
Red Flags: Only storage availability monitored; integrity check samples too narrow; failed object scope unknown; viewer lifecycle ignored; no restore test; archive exceptions aged; refresh occurs after support expiry; Quality not reviewing trends.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-14-018]: Demonstrate how post-retirement access is limited to current authorized roles, remains attributable, is periodically reviewed, and prevents alteration, bulk extraction, or administrator circumvention of retained GxP records.
Phase: 14 Decommission Retention | Domain: Access Management & Security | Topic: Post-retirement archive access | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Select one legacy administrator, former project member, vendor account, and service identity and prove termination or current justification across archive, storage, cloud, database, key vault, and backup layers.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Archive role design, named-user and service-account populations, approvals and reviews, leaver cleanup, privileged-access restrictions, immutable or write-protected controls, access and export logs, alerts, and exceptions. Acceptance requires least privilege, unique attribution, timely revocation, and independent monitoring.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7, 12, and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(c), 11.10(d), 11.10(e), and 11.10(g); GDPR Article 32 where personal data apply.
Red Flags: Project accounts remain; archive access not reviewed; shared administrator; write access unnecessary; exports unlogged; former supplier access active; lower storage or backup layer omitted; leaver process excludes archive.

metadata.reference: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7, 12, and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(c), 11.10(d), 11.10(e), and 11.10(g); GDPR Article 32 where personal data apply.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-14-019]: Demonstrate how encryption keys, signing certificates, trust chains, secrets, tokens, algorithms, and recovery material needed to access or verify retained records remain available, protected, attributable, and replaceable throughout retention.
Phase: 14 Decommission Retention | Domain: Cryptographic Lifecycle | Topic: Long-term keys, certificates, and secrets | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Simulate loss or expiry of the primary key or certificate and show the tested recovery, escrow, re-encryption, verification, and audit path without weakening access control or losing proof of historical signature validity.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Cryptographic dependency inventory, ownership, key and certificate lifecycle, escrow and backup, algorithm and expiry monitoring, recovery or re-encryption tests, access controls and logs, destruction rules, and technology-refresh plan. Acceptance requires tested continuity and no single undocumented key dependency.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7, 12, 16, and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(c) and 11.10(d); NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 SC and CP controls as nonbinding guidance.
Red Flags: Key owner unknown; single key copy; certificate expiry unmonitored; recovery untested; vendor key unavailable after contract; re-encryption changes provenance without control; destruction occurs before retention ends. Finding trigger: evidence is missing, unapproved, incomplete, inconsistent, or cannot be reproduced for the auditor-selected sample.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-14-020]: Demonstrate how personal data is minimized and deleted or anonymized when no longer lawfully required while regulated records, legal holds, audit trails, and evidentiary integrity remain protected.
Phase: 14 Decommission Retention | Domain: Data Privacy | Topic: Retention-limited deletion and minimization | Priority: High
Follow-Up Probe: Select one deletion request or expired personal-data class that intersects a GxP record and show the legal basis, field-level disposition, propagation to replicas and exports, and proof that the retained record remains complete and meaningful.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Data inventory and classification, lawful-basis and retention mapping, minimization and deletion rules, legal-hold checks, field-level design, anonymization validation where used, propagation to archives, replicas, and suppliers, execution logs, exceptions, and approvals. Acceptance requires lawful, consistent, and auditable disposition without loss of required GxP evidence.
Regulatory Alignment: GDPR Articles 5, 17, 25, 30, and 32 where applicable; EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7, 9, and 17; applicable predicate-rule retention requirements.
Red Flags: All data retained indefinitely as GxP; deletion breaks audit trail or attribution; replicas and supplier copies ignored; anonymization reversible or unvalidated; legal hold not checked; deletion evidence unavailable.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-14-021]: Account for every backup, replica, snapshot, export, staging area, test copy, disaster-recovery environment, and removable medium and demonstrate its approved retention, access restriction, migration, expiry, or destruction.
Phase: 14 Decommission Retention | Domain: Backup & Data Disposition | Topic: Residual copies and backup retirement | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Select a copy outside the primary production account or data center and prove who can restore it, which keys and software it needs, when it expires, how legal holds apply, and how destruction is verified.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Copy topology and inventory, backup and snapshot catalogues, DR and test environments, exports and media register, retention and hold rules, access, key dependencies, expiration or destruction jobs, certificates, and reconciliation. Acceptance requires complete accounting and no restorable uncontrolled copy.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7.2, 12, 16, and 17; 21 CFR 211.68(b); GDPR Articles 5 and 32 where personal data apply; NIST SP 800-88 Rev. 2 as nonbinding sanitization guidance.
Red Flags: Copy inventory incomplete; snapshots in personal or supplier account; no expiry; restore access retained broadly; legal hold not propagated; test copies forgotten; destruction claimed without verification; keys persist after data destruction.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-14-022]: Demonstrate the controlled sequence used to stop interfaces, jobs, APIs, file transfers, notifications, monitoring, user accounts, service accounts, certificates, tokens, remote support, and network routes without losing late data or leaving unauthorized pathways.
Phase: 14 Decommission Retention | Domain: Interface & Identity Shutdown | Topic: Orderly termination of technical pathways | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Show live telemetry after the claimed shutdown and explain any authentication attempt, network connection, scheduled execution, queue item, file arrival, or data write, including how it was contained and reconciled.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Shutdown plan and dependency order, cut-off and queue reconciliation, interface partner confirmation, job and account inventories, revocation and route changes, monitoring period, live telemetry, exceptions, and approvals. Acceptance requires zero unresolved traffic, active identity, or late data after final cut-off.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 5, 10, 12, 13, 16, and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(d), 11.10(g), and 11.300 where Part 11 applies.
Red Flags: Interfaces stopped before queues reconcile; service accounts active; certificates or tokens valid; late files discarded; network route remains; monitoring removed before observation period; partner not notified; live writes after shutdown.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-14-023]: Trace the supplier exit from contract obligations through complete data and metadata return, format usability, transition support, subprocessor coverage, access revocation, residual-copy destruction, evidence availability, and final service termination.
Phase: 14 Decommission Retention | Domain: Supplier Exit Management | Topic: Data return, continuity, and destruction | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Ask the supplier to account for primary, backup, replicated, support, telemetry, log, analytics, and subprocessor copies and compare the response with the shared-responsibility model and your own data-flow evidence.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Contract and Quality agreement exit clauses, data and copy inventory, export specification and reconciliation, transition and retrieval test, subprocessor attestations, access revocation, deletion or destruction certificate with scope and method, evidence and audit rights, and internal acceptance. Acceptance requires usable complete return and verified disposition of all residual copies.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 3, 7, 12, 16, and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(b) to 11.10(d) where Part 11 applies; GDPR Articles 28 and 32 where personal data apply.
Red Flags: Contract lacks usable export or deletion terms; proprietary format; audit trails or logs excluded; subprocessor copies unknown; deletion certificate generic; supplier access persists; transition support ends before acceptance; evidence inaccessible after termination. Finding trigger: evidence is missing, unapproved, incomplete, inconsistent, or cannot be reproduced for the auditor-selected sample.

content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-14-024]: Demonstrate that every retired asset and storage location was uniquely identified, removed from service and monitoring inventories at the correct time, sanitized or destroyed with verified results, and did not eliminate required archive or inspection access.
Phase: 14 Decommission Retention | Domain: Asset Disposal & Continuity | Topic: Sanitization, asset closure, and post-shutdown access | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Select one reused or cloud-abstracted asset and show the sanitization method, validation or verification, residual-data risk, chain of custody, CMDB update, and proof that no required record or recovery dependency was destroyed.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Asset and media inventory, disposition authorization, archive and dependency clearance, sanitization method and verification, chain of custody, destruction certificate, cloud provider evidence, CMDB and license updates, and post-shutdown retrieval test. Acceptance requires verified sanitization commensurate with sensitivity and preserved required access.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 Sections 7, 12, 16, and 17; GDPR Article 32 where personal data apply; NIST SP 800-88 Rev. 2 as nonbinding current sanitization guidance.
Red Flags: Asset list incomplete; generic destruction certificate; sanitization not verified; cloud resource identity unclear; chain of custody gap; required viewer or key destroyed; CMDB still active or removed before shutdown evidence; archive retrieval fails afterward.

document_title: Top 25 Checklists GxP IT Audit Questions 2026
content:
GxP IT Audit Checklist [DA-14-025]: Demonstrate that final decommissioning approval was based on complete migration or archive acceptance, reconciled records, resolved exceptions, terminated dependencies and access, governed residual copies, preserved inspection capability, updated inventories, and explicit long-term ownership.
Phase: 14 Decommission Retention | Domain: Decommissioning Closure | Topic: Final report and residual obligations | Priority: Critical
Follow-Up Probe: Choose the strongest unresolved exception or retained dependency at closure and show who accepted the residual risk, how it is monitored, when it expires, what event triggers reopening, and who funds corrective action after the project team disbands.
Expected Evidence / Criteria: Final decommissioning report, evidence index, source and target reconciliation, deviations and CAPA, retrieval and recovery acceptance, access and interface termination, supplier exit, backup and asset disposition, CMDB and inventory updates, residual-risk register, long-term owner and review schedule, and Quality approval. Acceptance requires no hidden critical dependency and durable governance after project closure.
Regulatory Alignment: EU GMP Annex 11 lifecycle principle and Sections 4.2, 7, 10, 12, 16, and 17; 21 CFR 11.10(b) to 11.10(e) where Part 11 applies; ICH Q9(R1) Sections 4.5 and 4.6.
Red Flags: Final approval predates evidence; open critical exceptions hidden; archive owner or budget absent; access or interface still active; inventory not updated; residual risk has no expiry or monitoring; source destroyed before verified retrieval; project disbands with open CAPA.
